- Send reminder texts and make reminder calls to families to keep attendance high.
- Provide support to students who are having issues with their devices.
- Support the Youth and Education team in collecting and maintaining student and family records, documents, and case notes, while maintaining confidentiality.
- Conduct outreach phone calls to invite families to participate in programs.
- Conduct enrollment sessions with new families to ensure they understand the program and to collect all necessary documentation.
- Provide ongoing support to volunteers, including problem-solving, answering questions, coaching, and sharing teaching and learning resources and best practices.

**In-home Tutoring Program**

title: Senior Youth Program Specialist
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***This position has an end date of August 31, 2027.***

**IRC Background:** IRC opened an office in Spokane in 2022 and provides a continuum of services including intensive case management, employment and economic empowerment services, immigration assistance, health and wellness programming, and education support to refugee and immigrant families in Washington State. IRC Spokane is committed to providing trauma-informed, equitable, and accessible services and maintaining and evolving a diverse, inclusive, and supportive workplace.

**Job Overview:** The vision of the IRC Washington Youth Program is that youth from refugee and immigrant backgrounds will have the skills and resources necessary to pursue a future of opportunity. The Youth and Education Program works towards this vision by providing educational and enrichment opportunities to help school-aged youth from refugee and immigrant backgrounds catch up on missed education, adjust to a new school, accelerate English language development, and build positive relationships in the school and community. This program supports school-age youth and their families, and also provides support to teachers and school administration to better connect and serve these students.

The Sr. Youth Program Specialist is responsible for teaching and implementation of IRC’s Youth and Education Programs in Spokane, WA.

The Virtual Ready to Read (VR2R) program promotes enjoyment of reading, literacy skills, language acquisition, social and emotional asset development, and positive cultural identity for students in grades 3–8. Upon enrollment, students receive a device, a learning kit with craft materials and art supplies, a workbook, and a set of books. Parents and students attend an orientation to ensure they know how to use their device and the video call platform. Each student attends one-hour online classes twice a week from January through May. Students read a book as a group and engage in themed lessons with vocabulary and grammar content, discussion questions, and craft activities. Students also take part in virtual field trips to institutions such as the Pacific Science Center, Woodland Park Zoo, and Seattle Aquarium. Two consecutive 1-hour classes are led by an IRC teacher on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 4:00 pm – 6:00 pm (a slightly later start at 4:15 pm can be accommodated if your schedule does not allow an earlier start). The program runs from January to May. Classes are small with typically under 15 students in attendance for each class.

The Individualized Tutoring Program matches K-12 students and families with an IRC-screened, trained, and supervised tutor who supports English language acquisition, literacy and fluency, math skills, general homework, and social-emotional learning. Tutors meet with students in their homes once a week after school for 1–2 hours over a period of 3–6 months. Tutoring is one of IRC’s long-standing programs, and IRC is committed to providing high-quality tutoring in alignment with the standards of Stanford University’s National Student Success Accelerator. title: [Re-Ad] Capacity Building Specialist (Public Health) – Philippines
body:
**A. About Asian Disaster Preparedness Center**

ADPC is an autonomous international organization established for scientific, educational, developmental, and humanitarian purposes with a vision of safer communities and sustainable development through disaster risk reduction and climate resilience in Asia and the Pacific and Africa. Established in 1986 as a technical capacity-building center, ADPC has grown and expanded its role to serve scientific, educational, developmental, and humanitarian purposes. ADPC employs a wide range of professional expertise typically required for Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and Climate Resilience (CR).

ADPC develops and implements cross-sectoral projects/programs on the strategic themes of Risk Knowledge and Geoinformatics, Policy and Institutional System, Effective Localization for Resilience, Climate Services, Resilient Planning and Implementation, Preparedness and Anticipatory Action, Nature based Solutions, Financing for Resilience, Resilient Recovery, Food and Water Security, Disaster Risk Finance Insurance, Health Risk Management, Urban & Infrastructure Resilience, Private Sector Engagement, and ADPC Knowledge Academy. Our strategic themes are complemented and underpinned by the cross-cutting themes of gender equality and social inclusion, disaster and climate innovations, and regional and transboundary cooperation.

Through its work, ADPC supports the implementation of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030, the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), the New Urban Agenda, the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, the agenda defined at the World Humanitarian Summit in 2016, and other relevant international frameworks.

For details, please refer to the ADPC website at http://www.adpc.net/.

**B. Department Introduction**

The Preparedness and Climate Action Department (PCA) strengthens the capacities of governments, response organizations, civil society, private sector actors, and at‑risk communities to prepare for, respond to, recover from disasters and adapt to the increasing risks associated with disasters and climate change. PCA emphasizes locally led preparedness and adaptation, ensuring that resilience-building efforts are rooted in local systems, institutions, knowledge, and leadership.

PCA contributes to ADPC’s regional mandate by designing and implementing programs aligned with ADPC’s strategic priority areas, including Climate Services, Preparedness and Anticipatory Action, Resilient Planning and Implementation, Health Risk Management, Nature‑based Solutions, Resilient Recovery, and Financing for Resilience, among others. These programs support countries in advancing the Sendai Framework, SDGs, and the Paris Agreement, while strengthening institutional, community, and system-wide resilience. The department also ensures that all interventions incorporate ADPC’s core cross‑cutting themes, Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI), Disaster and Climate Innovations, and Regional and Transboundary Cooperation, as foundational elements across program design, implementation, monitoring, and knowledge generation. PCA is structured into three functional units that work together to deliver integrated preparedness and climate action programming:

- **Climate Action and Impact (CAI) –** driving climate action strategies, impact measurement, monitoring and evaluation systems, and evidence generation.
- **Emergency Preparedness and Response (EPR)** – strengthening preparedness capacities, emergency response planning, and health risk management.
- **Resilience Building and Localization (RBL)** – supporting resilient recovery, localization approaches, and capacity development at national and subnational levels.

Through multi‑country operations, technical advisory services, and strategic partnerships, PCA ensures coherent, evidence‑based, and impact‑driven delivery of ADPC’s mandate across Asia and the Pacific.

**C. Statement of Intent**

The Asian Disaster Preparedness Center (ADPC) seeks to strengthen its regional programming and technical capacity for public health emergency preparedness and response across the Asia-Pacific region. Building on its experience in disaster preparedness, emergency response, regional cooperation, and multi-country program implementation, ADPC aims to strengthen its support to countries and communities in preparing for and responding to emerging and re-emerging infectious disease outbreaks and other public health emergencies. Effective public health emergency preparedness and response require timely and coordinated action, supported by strong technical and operational capacities, effective coordination mechanisms, and capable national and local response actors. Through partnerships with governments, regional institutions, UN agencies, civil society organizations, academic and research institutions, and technical networks, ADPC promotes nationally and locally led approaches that strengthen preparedness, response, and recovery capacities.

Within this broader commitment, ADPC is a consortium partner in the Local Engagement and Response Network (LEARN): Strengthening Localized Multi-Sectoral Readiness and Response to Infectious Disease Outbreaks in Humanitarian Settings, led by International Medical Corps (IMC). LEARN aims to strengthen Local First Responders (LFRs), particularly Local and National Non-Governmental Organizations (L/NNGOs), to improve their readiness and multisectoral response to infectious disease outbreaks of epidemic or pandemic potential in humanitarian settings.

As a consortium partner, ADPC will provide technical and implementation support for LEARN activities in South and Southeast Asia, including the Philippines. In the Philippines, ADPC will work closely with the IMC Philippines Country Team to provide technical support for capacity-strengthening activities, including contextualization of LEARN materials, training facilitation, organizational capacity strengthening, remote coaching and technical assistance to participating L/NNGOs. To support this work, ADPC seeks to engage a **Capacity Building Expert (Public Health) – Philippines**. The consultant will serve as ADPC’s technical capacity-strengthening and coordination focal point, working closely with the ADPC project team, the Health Emergency Management (HEM) Specialist, the IMC Philippines Country Team, participating L/NNGOs and relevant stakeholders to plan, deliver and follow up practical technical support within the agreed country implementation arrangements.

A key focus of the assignment will be to ensure that LEARN's capacity-strengthening approaches and resources are appropriately contextualized to the Philippine public health, humanitarian, disaster risk, and institutional context, and that participating L/NNGOs receive practical technical support to strengthen their readiness and capacity to respond to infectious disease outbreaks.

**Note:** *It is not the intent of the ToR to cover every aspect of the position requirements, rather to highlight the most important areas of personal and joint responsibilities.*

**D. Duties and Responsibilities**

Under the overall guidance of the Unit Head, Emergency Preparedness and Response/LEARN Program Lead of ADPC, the Capacity Building Expert will serve as ADPC’s technical capacity-strengthening and coordination focal point for LEARN activities in the Philippines. The consultant will work closely with participating L/NNGOs, relevant stakeholders, the ADPC project team and the IMC Philippines Country Team on day-to-day planning, implementation coordination, organizational engagement and follow-up, and translation of LEARN technical approaches into practical, context-appropriate support responsive to identified organizational and operational needs. The consultant will undertake the following key responsibilities:

**1. Technical and Capacity-Building Support**

- Provide technical expertise in public health emergency preparedness and response to support ADPC's technical contribution to LEARN implementation in the Philippines.
- Jointly plan capacity-strengthening activities with ADPC and the IMC Philippines Country Team, and undertake agreed technical preparation, contextualization, facilitation and follow-up of training, exercises and other capacity-development interventions for participating L/NNGOs and local first responders, in accordance with the approved workplan and country implementation arrangements.
- Adapt relevant LEARN training materials, tools and technical resources in consultation with the IMC Philippines Country Team, participating organizations and relevant stakeholders to reflect organizational capacities, priorities and Philippine realities; submit substantive technical products to the ADPC LEARN team for technical review and quality assurance before use, and incorporate agreed feedback.
- Support the review of English-to-Filipino/Tagalog and relevant local-language translations of LEARN training materials, tools and guidance for accuracy, clarity, consistency of public health terminology and suitability for participating organizations. Work with the IMC Philippines Country Team and qualified translators or language reviewers, drawing on the Consultant’s language competencies, and coordinate with project team to resolve technical ambiguities before use.
- Provide technical facilitation and resource support for agreed LEARN training and capacity-development activities, coordinating participant engagement, schedules, field access, event arrangements and logistical requirements with the IMC Philippines Country Team and ADPC according to their agreed responsibilities.
- Apply appropriate adult-learning, participatory and practical training methodologies to strengthen the application of knowledge and skills by participating organizations.
- Provide practical technical support according to assessed needs on infectious disease preparedness and response, including Rapid Response Teams (RRTs) or equivalent response mechanisms, health emergency management (HEM) systems, activation and escalation arrangements, emergency operations/incident coordination, community-based surveillance and reporting, risk communication and community engagement (RCCE), infection prevention and control (IPC), water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), referral pathways and multisectoral coordination.
- Apply the 7-1-7 framework as an additional ADPC technical framework, rather than an existing LEARN contractual requirement, with participating L/NNGOs and local first responders as appropriate to their roles and Philippine public health systems: detect a suspected infectious disease outbreak within seven days of emergence, notify the appropriate public health authority within one day of detection, and complete priority early response actions within seven days of notification.
- Integrate relevant 7-1-7 concepts into assessments, training, coaching and exercises with the IMC Philippines Country Team to identify bottlenecks and enabling factors in detection, notification and early response, and strengthen reporting, activation and coordination pathways. Organizational support will contribute to wider system performance within each organization’s mandate; the Consultant will not be responsible for measuring national 7-1-7 performance.

**2. Organizational Capacity Strengthening and Technical Assistance**

- Work closely with the IMC Philippines Country Team to plan and conduct the agreed technical components of organizational and readiness assessments using agreed tools; document baseline capacities, strengths and gaps, validate findings with participating L/NNGOs, and submit findings to project team for technical review to inform capacity-strengthening support.
- Translate validated assessment findings into organization-specific capacity-strengthening action plans with participating L/NNGOs and the IMC Philippines Country Team, identifying priorities, responsible persons, timelines, training and coaching requirements, and evidence of progress. Align implementation with the Program’s approved workplan, country implementation arrangements and available resources.
- Provide ongoing technical assistance, mentoring, practical exercises and remote or in-person just-in-time coaching, as appropriate and authorized, to participating organizations to implement agreed capacity-strengthening priorities and apply learning in their preparedness and response arrangements, coordinating support and follow-up with the IMC Philippines Country Team.
- Support L/NNGOs in developing, testing and updating organizational preparedness arrangements and community response plans, including roles and responsibilities, activation triggers, reporting and referral pathways, coordination and resource needs, based on assessed priorities.
- Monitor progress against organization-specific action plans through documented follow-up, evidence of practical application and reassessment where appropriate; identify additional coaching needs, support problem-solving, and escalate unresolved technical issues and operational constraints to the Program Lead and IMC Philippines focal point, as appropriate.
- Promote approaches that build on existing national and local systems, structures and capacities and support locally led preparedness and response.

**3. Stakeholder Engagement and Field Coordination**

- Coordinate regular technical engagement with participating L/NNGOs, local first responder networks, public health and humanitarian actors, community-based organizations and other relevant stakeholders in close collaboration with ADPC and the IMC Philippines Country Team, following agreed country engagement and communication arrangements.
- Jointly conduct participatory stakeholder mapping exercises with the IMC Philippines Country Team, building on existing country mapping, and periodically update the mapping of L/NNGOs, local first responders, community-based organizations, public health authorities, health facilities, surveillance and laboratory actors, humanitarian coordination mechanisms and technical partners relevant to approved project locations.
- Analyze stakeholder roles, capacities, geographic and population coverage, coordination relationships, referral and reporting pathways, and gaps or duplication to inform organizational screening, selection and onboarding recommendations and capacity-strengthening priorities.
- Support participating organizations in establishing or strengthening linkages with relevant national and subnational public health preparedness and response mechanisms, as appropriate
- Maintain an updated stakeholder map/database in coordination with the IMC Philippines Country Team, applying appropriate data protection procedures and sharing relevant information with ADPC.
- Maintain regular technical communication with participating organizations to identify emerging capacity needs and provide appropriate follow-up support.
- Contribute to consultations, technical discussions, workshops and other LEARN engagements as required.
- Provide contextual and technical updates to the ADPC LEARN team on public health emergency preparedness, disaster-health risks and other developments affecting capacity strengthening and project implementation in the Philippines.
- Facilitate peer learning among participating organizations in coordination with the IMC Philippines Country Team and participate in cross-site technical exchanges with the Thailand–Myanmar Border Capacity Building Expert, HEM Specialist and relevant LEARN partners to share tools, lessons and practical solutions while maintaining context-specific implementation.
- Contribute Philippine experience and lessons to the refinement of LEARN capacity-strengthening resources and approaches.

**4. Outbreak Readiness and Response Support**

- Maintain awareness of emerging infectious disease events and public health threats relevant to participating organizations and project locations through coordination with the IMC Philippines Country Team and appropriate public health information sources, and communicate significant developments and potential support needs to ADPC.
- Where an outbreak or other public health emergency creates a need for additional LEARN support, provide agreed technical and coordination assistance to participating L/NNGOs in close collaboration with the IMC Philippines Country Team, subject to ADPC/LEARN authorization, available resources, security considerations and defined project scope. Support will be coordinated with responsible public health authorities and relevant response mechanisms and remain within Consultant’s competencies and authorized role.
- Support rapid identification of organizational operational needs, capacities and gaps with IMC Philippines and participating organizations, and translate findings into priority actions. As authorized and appropriate, assist activation of RRTs or equivalent mechanisms, coordination, information management and reporting, community engagement, referral pathways, IPC/WASH and response planning; provide remote or field-based just-in-time coaching.
- Document operational bottlenecks, enabling factors and lessons from response support with IMC Philippines, applying 7-1-7 or Early Action Review principles where appropriate, and integrate agreed learning into organizational action plans, community response plans and subsequent preparedness activities.

**5. Monitoring, Documentation and Reporting**

- Monitor capacity-strengthening activities and organizational progress against agreed workplan milestones, action plans and LEARN indicators in coordination with the ADPC project team and IMC Philippines Country Team, using agreed country monitoring systems and reporting schedules.
- Maintain training attendance and participant profiles, learning assessments, exercise findings, mentoring/coaching logs, stakeholder mapping records, organizational action trackers, technical review records and evidence of follow-up, using agreed formats and safe data-management procedures. Coordinate record collection and consolidation with the IMC Philippines Country Team to avoid duplication and disaggregate participation data by sex, age and disability where feasible, appropriate and safe.
- Provide regular technical and implementation updates to ADPC and share relevant updates with the IMC Philippines Country Team through agreed reporting arrangements, including achievements, action-plan progress, challenges, emerging needs, agreed corrective actions and responsibilities for follow-up.
- Contribute technical inputs and supporting information to ADPC's periodic LEARN progress reports, monitoring requirements and other project documentation.
- Document feedback, lessons learned, capacity-development results, good practices and emerging technical needs from participating organizations and field implementation.
- Propose improvements to technical tools, learning resources and guidance based on assessment findings, implementation experience and feedback from participating organizations and the IMC Philippines Country Team, and submit substantive technical revisions to the HEM Specialist for review and quality assurance.
- Support continuous improvement of LEARN capacity-strengthening approaches and contribute Philippine experiences and lessons to cross-country learning and refinement of technical resources.

**6. Cross-Cutting Responsibilities**

- Integrate Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI), safeguarding, conflict sensitivity and do-no-harm principles throughout stakeholder engagement, organizational assessments, training, coaching, community response planning and monitoring.
- Facilitate safe, inclusive and accessible participation, taking into account language, disability-related needs, displacement-related barriers and other relevant contextual considerations.
- Protect confidential organizational and community information, apply appropriate data protection and information-sharing procedures, and report safeguarding concerns through established ADPC and partner mechanisms.
- Undertake other related technical and capacity-strengthening responsibilities as may be reasonably required to support effective implementation of LEARN in the Philippines.

**E. Working Principles**

In performing the duties and responsibilities outlined above, the Consultant will report directly to the LEARN Program Lead, who will provide overall programmatic, contractual and management oversight, including workplan and budget management, coordination with IMC, and approval of major implementation decisions. For country-level implementation, the Consultant will work in close coordination with the IMC Philippines Country Team on activity planning, organizational engagement, implementation arrangements, technical delivery and follow-up, in accordance with agreed partner responsibilities and coordination mechanisms.

**F. Required Qualifications**

***Required Qualifications and Specifications***

**Education:**

- Advanced university degree (Master's degree preferred) in Public Health, Epidemiology, Global Health, Health Emergency/Disaster Management, Community Health, International Development, or another relevant field.
- A Bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline combined with substantial relevant professional experience may be considered.

**Professional Experience:**

- At least 8 years of relevant professional experience in public health, humanitarian health, infectious disease preparedness and response, health emergency management, community health, disaster preparedness or a closely related field.
- Demonstrated experience in capacity strengthening, training facilitation, mentoring and/or coaching of local organizations, health workers or community-based responders.
- Practical experience in infectious disease outbreak preparedness and/or response, public health emergency management or related programming.
- Proven experience working with government/public health institutions, health emergency coordination mechanisms, local government structures, NGOs and technical partners in the Philippines.
- Demonstrated experience working with local and national NGOs, civil society organizations and/or community-based organizations.
- Experience conducting or supporting organizational/capacity assessments and translating identified gaps into capacity-development interventions.
- Experience facilitating participatory, competency-based and/or scenario-based training is highly desirable.
- Experience with Rapid Response Teams (RRTs), emergency operations, community-based surveillance, risk communication and community engagement, IPC/WASH, community response planning or related technical areas would be an advantage.
- Knowledge of contemporary outbreak readiness and response frameworks, including 7-1-7, is highly desirable. Experience supporting real-time outbreak response, RRTs, emergency operations/incident coordination, Early Action Reviews, after-action reviews or comparable operational learning processes would be an advantage.
- Experience working across the disaster–health nexus, including preparedness and response in areas affected by natural hazards and concurrent public health emergencies, would be an advantage.
- Demonstrated knowledge and experience of the Philippine public health emergency preparedness and response context, including national and/or subnational systems, is strongly preferred.
- Experience working with organizations or stakeholders in Luzon/NCR and/or Mindanao/BARMM would be an advantage.

**Language**

- Excellent written and spoken English is required.
- Professional proficiency in Filipino/Tagalog is highly desirable.
- Knowledge of relevant local languages in project implementation areas would be an advantage.

**G. Performance Competency**

**Core competencies**

- **Integrity:** Demonstrates the highest level of commitment and demonstrates respect for persons of concern to ADPC, partners, and colleagues in all aspects of work. Ensures that personal and professional behavior is of the highest standard.
- **Diversity Awareness:** Able to embrace the uniqueness of all individuals along several dimensions such as race, religious beliefs, ethnicity, age, gender, physical abilities, political beliefs, socioeconomic status, disability, political conviction, or any other distinguishing features.
- **Equality Awareness:** Understands that each individual has an equal opportunity to make decisions, participate in social activities, perform any work at the organization, and make the most of her/ his life and talents.
- **Teamwork and Collaboration:** Works constructively within and across teams in ways that allow shared objectives to be achieved. Works effectively with colleagues and partners. Fosters a positive and collaborative environment.

**H. Preparedness and Climate Action Department Functional Competencies:**

- **Teamwork and collaboration:** Works constructively within and across teams in ways that allow shared objectives to be achieved. Works effectively with colleagues and partners. Fosters a positive and collaborative environment.
- **Results Orientation:** Focuses on delivering agreed-upon results through effectively managing internal and external resources to achieve results. Demonstrates a commitment to both personal and organizational excellence, with an emphasis on results.
- **Analytical Problem-Solving Skills:** Displays analytical thinking by identifying, defining, and analyzing information, situations, and problems. Arrives at viable solutions through a variety of approaches. Demonstrates critical thoughts, methodical review of implications, intuition, and rational conclusions.
- **Adaptability:** Demonstrates flexibility, both intellectually and behaviorally, to adapt to and work effectively in various situations, often under demanding conditions, and to cope with the unforeseen or unexpected. Looks for opportunities presented by change and is not "paralyzed" by new and unusual scenarios. Creates opportunities to improve how they work.

**I. Duty Station**

Manila, Philippines. Technical support will cover participating L/NNGOs and approved LEARN project locations in the Philippines. Specific locations, remote support and field missions will be agreed through the approved workplan in close coordination with the IMC Philippines Country Team; travel requires ADPC authorization, available resources, appropriate access and security arrangements, and alignment with project scope.

**J. Duration**

November 2026 – September 2027 (11 months)

**K. Itinerary**

During official missions outside the duty station, the Consultant will be entitled to local/international travel, daily subsistence allowance, accommodation, and other related travel costs as per ADPC financial policy.

**L. Condition of payment**

The Consultant will receive a monthly payment upon submission of completed timesheets. In addition, the Consultant is eligible for reimbursement of any program-related expenses incurred in the implementation of project activities, subject to the prior approval of the Program Lead.

title: Haiti-Based Sectoral and Technical Experts and Trainers
body:
**Position:** Sectoral Technical Experts / Trainers - Haiti  
**Type:** Consultancy / Project-based / Roster  
**Location:** Haiti  
**Organization:** STOOS Consulting

**STOOS Consulting** is inviting qualified **sectoral technical experts, trainers, facilitators, researchers, and consultants in Haiti** to join its roster for upcoming humanitarian, development, research, assessment, capacity building, monitoring, evaluation, and third-party monitoring opportunities across the country.

This call is open to experienced professionals from different technical backgrounds who are interested in supporting future assignments with **UN agencies, INGOs, NGOs, donors, development partners, local organizations, and community-based actors**.

**About STOOS Consulting**

**STOOS Consulting** is an international consulting firm specialized in **Third-Party Monitoring, MEAL, research and assessments, evaluations, data collection, capacity building, conflict and gender analysis, market systems research, and economic empowerment studies**. STOOS works in complex humanitarian and development contexts to produce practical, field-based, and evidence-driven findings that support programme quality, accountability, learning, and decision-making.

Through its network of national and international experts, STOOS supports assignments in areas such as **needs assessments, baseline and endline studies, final evaluations, outcome monitoring, technical training, capacity building, qualitative and quantitative research, community consultations, and field monitoring**.

**Profile of Experts Sought**

STOOS is looking to expand its Haiti roster with qualified experts and trainers in a wide range of sectors, including but not limited to **WASH, health, nutrition, protection, GBV, child protection, education, food security and livelihoods, climate resilience, disaster risk reduction, shelter, social protection, TVET, economic empowerment, migration, gender, disability inclusion, peacebuilding, conflict sensitivity, and MEAL**.

STOOS also welcomes applications from experts with experience in **research design, qualitative and quantitative data collection, training facilitation, curriculum development, institutional capacity building, market assessments, youth employment, entrepreneurship, community engagement, safeguarding, accountability to affected populations, and humanitarian/development programme quality**.

**Main Areas of Work**

Selected experts may be contacted for future assignments involving **technical training, capacity building, sectoral assessments, programme evaluations, field research, tool development, data collection supervision, contextual analysis, report writing, quality assurance, and technical advisory support**.

Depending on the opportunity, experts may support **KIIs, FGDs, surveys, community consultations, workshops, technical reviews, training delivery, data analysis, and preparation of practical recommendations** tailored to the Haiti context.

**Haiti Context and Relevant Experience**

Candidates with strong knowledge of Haiti's humanitarian and development context are encouraged to apply, especially those with experience related to **humanitarian response, disaster preparedness and response, earthquakes, hurricanes, flooding, climate resilience, displacement, protection risks, public health, nutrition, WASH, education, food security and livelihoods, social protection, gender equality, disability inclusion, migration, and community resilience**.

Experience working with communities in **urban, rural, coastal, earthquake-affected, hurricane-affected, displacement-affected, insecurity-affected, or hard-to-reach areas** is highly valued. STOOS particularly welcomes experts who can work respectfully with **women, youth, children, persons with disabilities, internally displaced people, migrants, returnees, farmers, fisherfolk, low-income households, and other vulnerable groups**.

**Key Skills and Qualifications**

Candidates should have relevant professional experience in one or more technical sectors and a strong understanding of the **Haiti context**, including local institutions, community structures, civil society actors, access and security dynamics, disaster risk management systems, and humanitarian/development priorities.

Applicants are encouraged to apply if they have worked with **UN agencies, INGOs, NGOs, local organizations, government partners, donor-funded programmes, academic institutions, consulting firms, or community-based initiatives**.

Strong candidates will demonstrate practical experience in **training, facilitation, technical advisory work, assessments, monitoring and evaluation, field research, community engagement, or programme implementation**.

Knowledge of **Do No Harm, safeguarding, PSEA, child protection, gender sensitivity, disability inclusion, ethical research, confidentiality, conflict sensitivity, and accountability to affected populations** is highly desirable.

Experience using digital tools such as **KoboToolbox, ODK, SurveyCTO, Excel, SPSS, Power BI, NVivo, or similar platforms** is considered an asset, depending on the assignment.

**Language Skills**

Fluency in **Haitian Creole** is required for most field-based and community-level assignments.

Good working knowledge of **French** is strongly preferred, especially for assignments involving technical reports, donor documentation, training materials, data analysis, and communication with international teams.

Knowledge of **English and/or Spanish** is a strong advantage, particularly for assignments requiring communication with regional or international stakeholders.

title: Oficial de Cadena de Abastecimiento y Compras
body:
El Consejo Danés para Refugiados (DRC por sus siglas en inglés) es una de las principales ONG humanitarias del mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para proporcionar asistencia adecuada con un enfoque basado en derechos para los refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, los desplazados internos, repatriados y migrantes. DRC ha estado presente en Colombia desde 2011, pero 2018 amplía sus operaciones en respuesta a la crisis venezolana. Actualmente DRC Colombia implementa una respuesta humanitaria centrada protección para refugiados y migrantes venezolanos y colombianos retornados en ciudades de Colombia como Riohacha, Barranquilla y Bogotá, actualmente también incorpora actividades en Nariño y en Norte de Santander.

**DESCRIPCIÓN GENERAL DEL CARGO:**

El Oficial de Cadena de Abastecimiento y Compras es responsable de las compras requeridas en las bases, así como de la debida gestión de los activos, manejo del inventario, almacenamiento, transporte de bienes y personas, gestión de flotas de vehículos y apoyo logístico general al programa general en Ocaña Norte de Santander y municipios asignados de conformidad con el marco interno de Danish Refugee Council – DRC y las regulaciones impuestas por los donantes.

**Responsabilidades:**

**Compras**

- Garantizar la correcta ejecución de los procesos competitivos de compras para todas las solicitudes requeridas en la base.
- Realizar procesos de compras para la generación de acuerdos marco según la necesidad identificada en el plan de compras de la base.
- Asegurar la recepción de compras requeridas para el adecuado funcionamiento de las operaciones de DRC en Norte de Santander y municipios asignados.
- Colaboración directa con los equipos de programa para la planificación local de las necesidades de compra y logísticas de los programas de DRC.
- Realizar seguimiento y control de todas las solicitudes de compras.
- Asegurar el respaldo documental de todos los procesos de compras en sharepoint, con el fin de asegurar transparencia y trazabilidad en nuestros procesos de compras.
- Correcto registro de proveedores locales de acuerdo con los lineamientos de DRC
- Gestionar el desarrollo e implementación de contratos marco y estrategias de abastecimiento que generen eficiencias operativas para la base.
- Monitorear el avance de los procesos de compras en la base e identificar cuellos de botella o riesgos operativos, proponiendo medidas correctivas.

**Logística**

- Asegurar la entrega oportuna de los materiales solicitados, teniendo en cuenta los procesos y tiempos establecidos por DRC.
- Garantizar la gestión de los servicios generales para los equipos de trabajo (alojamiento, personal, visitantes, oficinas, lugares de almacenamiento y seguridad).
- Coordinar con el equipo de seguridad para asegurar una distribución logística acorde con las condiciones operacionales y de contexto.
- Planificar y asegurar la disponibilidad de kits humanitarios para respuesta de emergencia en los programas de DRC.
- Brindar soporte logístico a las operaciones de la base y a los municipios asignados, garantizando el cumplimiento de los procedimientos internos y los requerimientos de los donantes.
- Apoyar el mantenimiento y adecuado funcionamiento de las instalaciones de DRC en Ocaña, Norte de Santander y municipios asignados.
- Implementar mecanismos de control, seguimiento y verificación de los bienes y elementos asignados al personal y a los programas.
- Apoyar los procesos de verificación física, auditorías internas y revisiones operativas relacionadas con la gestión logística cuando sea requerido.

**Gestión de Inventarios y Activos**

- Control, seguimiento y aseguramiento del inventario de kits humanitarios de DRC en Ocaña, Norte de Santander y municipios asignados.
- Control, registro y seguimiento de los activos fijos gestionados en la oficina local.
- Realizar inventarios periódicos y llevar el control detallado del inventario general de DRC.
- Implementación de mecanismos de control, conciliación y seguimiento de inventarios.
- Identificar riesgos, inconsistencias o desviaciones en la gestión de activos e inventarios, recomendando e implementando acciones correctivas y preventivas.
- Asegurar que toda la información relacionada con inventarios y activos esté actualizada y alineada con las directrices de Oficina Nacional y los donantes en el sistema ERP Dynamics.
- Asegurar el registro oportuno, la trazabilidad y la disponibilidad de los activos fijos, reportando y documentando cualquier incidente, pérdida, daño o baja de activos.
- Realizar verificaciones físicas periódicas de los activos y conciliarlas con los registros del sistema.
- Garantizar el adecuado respaldo documental de los movimientos de inventario y activos, asegurando transparencia, trazabilidad y cumplimiento de auditorías internas y externas.
- Coordinar las transferencias, asignaciones, préstamos y bajas de activos de acuerdo con las políticas y procedimientos vigentes de DRC.

**Gestión de Flota**

- Asegurar el cumplimiento de los procesos de gestión de flota de DRC en Ocaña, Norte de Santander y municipios asignados.
- Garantizar la disponibilidad de los vehículos requeridos para la ejecución de las actividades programáticas y operacionales.
- Coordinar las revisiones periódicas, mantenimientos preventivos y correctivos de los vehículos, y reportar oportunamente cualquier novedad o falla identificada.
- Mantener actualizada toda la documentación legal y operativa de la flota, gestionando oportunamente renovaciones de seguros, SOAT, revisiones técnico-mecánicas, permisos y demás requisitos aplicables.
- Monitorear el uso y consumo de combustible de la flota de la oficina local, identificando desviaciones y proponiendo acciones correctivas cuando sea necesario.
- Realizar seguimiento periódico a los logbooks y demás registros de flota, verificando la calidad de la información registrada, analizando tendencias de uso, kilometraje, consumo y mantenimiento para anticipar riesgos y establecer medidas correctivas o preventivas.
- Garantizar que los expedientes físicos y digitales de los vehículos se encuentren completos, organizados y disponibles para procesos de auditoría interna y externa.
- Promover el cumplimiento de las políticas de seguridad vial y uso adecuado de los vehículos por parte de los conductores y usuarios autorizados.

**Administración**

- Colaboración con la unidad de finanzas para el correcto registro de la cadena de abastecimiento.
- Coordinación con la unidad de finanzas para la oportuna ejecución de los pagos.
- Otras actividades que requiera la organización relacionada con la gestión logística en Ocaña, Norte de Santander y municipios asignados.

**EXPERIENCIA Y COMPETENCIAS TÉCNICAS:**

- Mínimo 2 años de experiencia en logística humanitaria, adquisiciones, transporte y distribución, almacenamiento y gestión de stocks para emergencias humanitarias.
- Buena comprensión de las normas y regulaciones de adquisiciones de los principales donantes internacionales.
- Buen conocimiento de la normatividad local a nivel de contrataciones.
- Excelentes conocimientos de MS Word, Excel y PowerPoint.
- Dominio intermedio de inglés será un valor agregado en el proceso.
- Capacidad analítica y resolutiva.
- Conocimiento avanzado en manejo de ERP´s
- Capacidad de gestión, proactividad, organización y atención al detalle.
- Habilidades de comunicación, calidez y amabilidad, orientación al servicio.

**Requisitos en términos de Formación Académica y conocimientos técnicos:**

Título Universitario pertinente en logística, administración de empresas y / o gestión de la cadena de suministro o carreras afines.

**Idiomas:**

• Castellano (obligatorio)

**Todas las funciones de DRC requieren que el titular domine las competencias básicas de DRC:**

- Lograr la excelencia: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes
- Colaboración: involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación
- Tomar la iniciativa: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación
- Comunicar: escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad
- Demostración de integridad: actuar de acuerdo con la visión y los valores de DRC

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONG's a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Medicina prepagada, cubrimiento del 100% de la póliza para el empleado y precio especial para beneficiarios.
- Contrato nacional a término fijo a 6 meses con todas las prestaciones de ley posibilidad, con posibilidad de renovación de contrato de acuerdo con desempeño y disponibilidad de fondos.
- Salario iniciando en $ 3.502.000 según experiencia y competencias del candidato.
- Fecha de inicio: Noviembre 2026
- Salario y condiciones de acuerdo con los términos de empleo en Colombia.

**Proceso de solicitud**

Todos los solicitantes deben subir únicamente una carta de presentación (1 página) y una hoja de vida actualizada (que no supere las 3 páginas) no se reciben más soportes por este medio.

**Fecha de cierre de solicitudes:** 13 de Noviembre de 2026 a las 11:59 am Hora Local

***Nota: Esta vacante está sujeta a subordinación de fondos por parte del donante.***

**¡Queremos que hagas parte de nuestro equipo!**

**En DRC creemos que la diversidad fortalece nuestros equipos y que cada persona aporta habilidades, experiencias y perspectivas valiosas. Por ello, invitamos especialmente a personas con movilidad reducida que cumplan con el perfil del cargo a postularse y participar en nuestros procesos de selección.**

**Nuestro compromiso es evaluar a cada candidato por sus competencias, experiencia y potencial. Si durante el proceso de selección requieres algún ajuste razonable o apoyo para participar en igualdad de condiciones, te invitamos a informárnoslo. Estaremos encantados de brindarte el acompañamiento necesario para que puedas participar plenamente.**

***Si usted aplica, se da por entendido que tiene disponibilidad inmediata para trabajar y tiene la posibilidad de desplazarse ocasionalmente a las zonas de intervención de la organización. Tenga en cuenta que las solicitudes se revisarán continuamente y las entrevistas se planificarán tan pronto como se identifique a un(a) candidato(a) adecuado(a). DRC se reserva el derecho a cerrar la vacante antes de la fecha límite una vez se identifique a un candidato idóneo. Se recomienda hacer la aplicación a esta vacante lo más pronto posible, si esta es de su interés.***

title: Research Manager
source: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
body:
## **BACKGROUND ON REACH**

REACH is an initiative of Acted whose purpose is to promote and facilitate the development of information products that enhance the humanitarian community’s decision making and planning capacity for emergency, reconstruction and development contexts. REACH facilitates information management for aid actors through three complementary services: (a) need and situation assessments facilitated by REACH teams; (b) situation analysis using satellite imagery; (c) provision of related database and (web)-mapping facilities and expertise.

**We are currently looking for a Research Manager to lead our research team in Somalia, based in Mogadishu.**

**Department**: REACH

**Position**: Research Manager

**Contract duration**: 1 year, with possibility of extension

**Location**: Mogadishu, Somalia

**Starting Date**: 1 January 2027.

## **Country profile**

Somalia remains within a complex and protracted crisis due to active conflict, the presence of non-state armed actors, the persistent presence of communicable diseases and climate-driven onset shocks – including droughts and flooding. Conflict and natural disasters continue to drive displacement and constrain the availability of resources, while the presence of armed groups severely impedes the level of access and support provided by humanitarian actors. The combination of restricted access to resources, drought, and flooding further exacerbates the possibility for outbreaks of communicable diseases like measles, cholera, and acute watery diarrhea.

Against this backdrop, REACH has developed a wide range of research cycles to provide an evidence base for the humanitarian community in Somalia. Data collected and disseminated by REACH aims to directly inform humanitarian response planning, as well as highlight areas of highest need and concern as crises emerge. Key areas of focus include:

**Multi-Sector Needs Assessment (MSNA):** REACH conducts the annual MSNA, whose findings feed into the Joint Intersectoral Analysis Framework (JIAF) workshop and, through it, the annual Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP).

**Food Security and Nutrition:** REACH conducts food security and nutrition assessments that feed into Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) Acute Food Insecurity and Acute Malnutrition analyses.

**Cash and Markets:** REACH provides research and analytical support to the Somali Cash Consortium and conducts market monitoring analysis as part of a harmonised approach, led by the Cash Working Group.

**Ad-hoc Research:** REACH conducts ad-hoc assessments as needs arise, including rapid needs assessments following sudden-onset shocks such as flooding, drought and conflict-induced displacement.

To ensure that research findings meaningfully inform humanitarian response planning, REACH shares data through formal coordination platforms, including the Inter-Cluster Coordination Group (ICCG), needs analysis and planning processes, the IPC Technical Working Group and the Cash Working Group, among others. Partner feedback is actively integrated to validate and triangulate findings, as well as to guide research design and geographic targeting.

## **FUNCTIONS**

REACH is seeking an experienced candidate who has previously managed teams and implemented projects in a complex humanitarian setting. Under the line management of the Deputy Country Representative, and in close coordination with the Country Representative and HQ, the Research Manager will be responsible for overseeing the implementation, development, and strategy of the research portfolio of the REACH Somalia mission. This includes managing the teams responsible for the MSNA, food security and nutrition assessments, the Somali Cash Consortium, market monitoring, and ad-hoc assessments such as rapid needs assessments.

The candidate should be comfortable representing REACH with donors and be able to coordinate and liaise with a range of senior external partners, including OCHA, cluster coordinators, UN agencies and NGOs. This position requires a profile that can be both analytical and managerial, as the Research Manager’s job can range from coordinating with external partners (whether data actor, humanitarian cluster, or donor) to analytical oversight of research products.

## **RESPONSIBILITIES**

The Research Manager’s responsibilities include the following:

***STAFF MANAGEMENT***

- Direct management of international and national research staff across the MSNA, food security and nutrition, cash and markets, and ad-hoc assessment workstreams, including recruitment, appraisals, and capacity building;
- Day-to-day management of the research team, including the development of work plans and performance indicators, and development and implementation of capacity training plans to improve efficiency and performance;
- Conduct regular check-ins with staff within the unit, and promote team building, productivity and staff welfare as the main pastoral focal point for research staff;
- Provide regular support and technical backstopping;
- Take on additional work streams and management responsibilities as well as advise in strategic mission decision-making as a member of the Senior Management Team (SMT), as required.

***RESEARCH CYCLE MANAGEMENT***

- Ensure that all research cycles are planned in line with the country strategy, relevant project and programme objectives, and REACH’s research cycle guidelines;
- Ensure that all (Senior) Research Officers are comprehensively briefed on objectives and expected outputs of research cycles, and that the overall implementation strategy of any given activity is clearly understood;
- Ensure that required secondary data review and/or analysis has been conducted in preparation for an assessment;
- For each research cycle, review ToRs before they are sent to HQ for validation and ensure that ToRs are validated before data collection begins;
- Ensure relevant stakeholders and partners are engaged in assessment design and planning, data collection, and management;
- Monitor data collection, ensuring correct implementation in line with agreed ToRs, and keep track of progress and delays of all assessments throughout the research cycle;
- Work closely with the Field Manager and Ops teams to ensure logistics, finance, administration, security and HR processes directly related to REACH are appropriately implemented, alongside the relevant Acted departments.

***PORTFOLIO OVERSIGHT***

- Oversee the timely delivery of the annual MSNA, ensuring that findings are available in time to feed into the JIAF workshop and the HNRP, and support the team in preparing for and participating in the JIAF process;
- Oversee food security and nutrition assessments, ensuring that methodologies, timelines and outputs are aligned with IPC requirements and that data is made available to IPC analyses as planned;
- Oversee REACH’s research support to the Somali Cash Consortium, ensuring that deliverables meet consortium and donor requirements and timelines;
- Oversee market monitoring analysis, ensuring consistent, timely outputs that are used by Cash Working Group partners;
- Lead the planning and rapid deployment of ad-hoc assessments, such as rapid needs assessments, in response to emerging crises and partner information needs, in coordination with OCHA and the clusters.

***ANALYSIS AND DISSEMINATION MANAGEMENT***

- Ensure research staff maintain regular communication with HQ on progress and deadlines for written products;
- Ensure the drafting of timely and accurate outputs (i.e. reports, factsheets, briefs, presentations, etc.), complying with REACH’s guidelines and quality standards;
- Review all research products before they are sent to HQ for validation and ensure that all written products are validated by HQ before external release;
- Under supervision of HQ, ensure that research products are uploaded to relevant data portals, as specified in research ToRs;
- Under the direction of the Country Representative and Deputy Country Representative, engage in the dissemination of research products, including emails, presentations to coordination bodies, and bilateral meetings, such as with donors;
- Support the Country Representative and Deputy Country Representative in conducting monitoring and evaluation as specified in the research ToRs and in line with REACH guidelines.

***STRATEGY DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION***

- With the Country Representative and Deputy Country Representative, identify information gaps in line with humanitarian priorities in Somalia, and identify advocacy and dissemination strategies to strengthen the impact of REACH’s work;
- Lead on formalising synergies with other assessment and knowledge management actors, as well as strategic partnerships with key humanitarian stakeholders and decision makers;
- As a member of the Senior Management Team (SMT), contribute to the development and implementation of the REACH Somalia country strategy.

***EXTERNAL ENGAGEMENT***

- Represent REACH at the Inter-Cluster Coordination Group (ICCG) and in other inter-agency coordination forums, and act as a key REACH focal point for OCHA on needs analysis and humanitarian programme cycle processes;
- Represent REACH in cluster and multi-sector meetings and technical working groups, including the IPC Technical Working Group and the Cash Working Group, and follow up on technical issues identified in these forums;
- In coordination with the Country Representative and Deputy Country Representative, present research findings to relevant partners to enhance their use and impact;
- Ensure that external communications with partners and key stakeholders, including UN agencies, local and national authorities, and NGOs, are conducted and documented as appropriate;
- Support the Country Representative and Deputy Country Representative in external engagement on REACH strategy and, when requested, in fundraising and grants management.

***DATA CONFIDENTIALITY AND PROTECTION***

- The Research Manager will maintain the strictest confidentiality on all data collected and related processes, ensuring full compliance with REACH’s data protection policy and SOPs, and will ensure that the research team does the same. They will actively take measures to prevent the unauthorized sharing of any information and data belonging to REACH and its partners or collected during their assignment with REACH.

The Research Manager is also responsible for ensuring that all interactions with crisis-affected populations are conducted in a respectful and consultative manner, and that communities are adequately consulted and informed about REACH programme objectives, activities and methodologies.

## **REQUIREMEnTS**

- **Academic qualifications** Excellent academic qualifications, including a Master’s degree in a relevant discipline (e.g. international relations, development, humanitarian response, data science, political science, statistics, social research, or similar).
- **Years of work experience** At least 3-5 years of relevant working experience in a humanitarian setting, such as assessments, monitoring and evaluation, research design and analysis.
- **Management experience** Previous experience in a management role in an INGO at field level. Track record in successful management of international and national teams in humanitarian contexts.
- **Research skills** Strong quantitative and qualitative research experience, including sampling, methodology design and analysis. Ability to provide technical oversight of research products to a high standard.
- **Familiarity with the humanitarian and aid system** Good understanding of the aid system and the research community. Experience with the humanitarian programme cycle (HNRP/JIAF) and with humanitarian coordination forums (e.g. ICCG, clusters) is strongly preferred.
- **Thematic experience** Prior experience with MSNA-type research, food security and nutrition assessments and/or IPC processes, and cash and markets research is highly desirable.
- **Communication/reporting skills** Excellent communication and drafting skills for effective reporting, including proven experience in contributing to high-level presentations and briefings to senior external audiences.
- **Software skills** Proven knowledge of the Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Skills in R, SPSS and/or STATA or other statistical analysis software are an advantage.
- **Multi-tasking skills** Ability to manage multiple research cycles in parallel with tight deadlines in a complex environment.
- **Level of independence** A self-starter with a proven ability to work independently.
- **Cross-cultural work environment** Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment.
- **Experience in geographical region** Past experience in the Horn of Africa region is desirable, or in any other emergency context where access is challenging.
- **Language skills** Fluency in English required, competency in Somali an asset.
- **Security environment** Openness to working in a high-risk security zone required. Ability to operate in a complex and challenging security environment. Ability to prioritize self-care and well-being.

## **COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

- For this position, salary between 3’660 **CHF** and 3’720 **CHF** monthly (before income tax), as well as a monthly living allowance of 300 **USD**
- NB - REACH salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.
- Accommodation and food provided in a guesthouse. REACH is hosted by Acted in Somalia.
- Enrolment in Swiss private pension fund (Swisslife – approx. 9.975% of staff gross salary), health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance
- Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered)
- R&R after 2-3 months (flight ticket up to 500$ + 200$ of living allowance)
- Contribution to the luggage transportation: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance)
- Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable.
- Predeparture induction - 3 days at HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in Acted HQ in Paris, including a 4-day in situ security training
- Enrolment in the Research Foundational Learning Programme within the first 3 months from the start of contract.
- REACH prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees

title: Senior Research Officer
source: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
body:
## **BACKGROUND ON IMPACT AND REACH**

REACH was born in 2010 as a joint initiative of two International NGOs ([IMPACT Initiatives](http://www.impact-initiatives.org/) and [ACTED](http://www.acted.org/)) and the United Nations Operational Satellite Applications Programme ([UNOSAT](http://www.unitar.org/unosat/)). REACH’s **purpose** is to promote and facilitate the development of information products that enhance the humanitarian community’s decision making and planning capacity for emergency, reconstruction and development contexts. REACH facilitates information management for aid actors through three complementary services: (a) need and situation assessments facilitated by REACH teams; (b) situation analysis using satellite imagery; (c) provision of related database and (web)-mapping facilities and expertise.

IMPACT Initiatives is a humanitarian NGO, based in Geneva, Switzerland. The organisation manages several initiatives, including the REACH Initiative. The IMPACT team comprises specialists in data collection, management and analysis and GIS. IMPACT was launched at the initiative of ACTED, an international NGO whose headquarter is based in Paris and is present in thirty countries. The two organizations have a strong complementarity formalized in a global partnership, enabling IMPACT to benefit from ACTED’s operational support on its fields of intervention.

**We are currently looking for a Senior Research Officer to support our team in Somalia.**

**Department**:REACH

**Position**:Senior Research Officer

**Contract duration**:4 months, with high likelihood of extension

**Location**: Mogadishu

**Starting Date**: 7 September 2026

## **COUNTRY PROFILE**

Somalia remains within a complex and protracted crisis due to active conflict, the presence of non-state armed actors, the persistent presence of communicable diseases and climate-driven onset shocks – including droughts and flooding. Conflict and natural disasters continue to drive displacement and constrain the availability of resources, while the presence of armed groups severely impedes the level of access and support provided by humanitarian actors. The combination of restricted access to resources, drought, and flooding further exacerbates the possibility for outbreaks of communicable diseases like measles, cholera, and acute watery diarrhea (AWD).

Against this backdrop, IMPACT Initiatives has developed a wide range of research cycles to provide an evidence-base for the humanitarian community. This includes the Multi-Sectoral Needs Assessment (MSNA), the Area-Based Analysis Platform aimed at supporting Area-Based Coordination, support to the Somali Cash Consortium, among others.

## **FUNCTIONS**

Under the line management of the Research Manager, the Senior Research Officer is responsible for the implementation of IMPACT’s MSNA research cycle in Somalia, including the preparation, data collection, analysis, drafting, dissemination, and evaluation stages. Throughout the MSNA, the Senior Research Officer engages with partners and stakeholders to promote their participation and maximize their impact. They also ensure an efficient and transparent use of resources required for project implementation.

This position requires strong research skills (particularly in quantitative and mixed methodology sampling), willingness to work in hardship location, an analytical mind, creativity, independence, and an interest in the national and regional context. Candidates should have strong writing and presentation skills and be able to clearly think through and articulate implications of research findings, as well as engage with external stakeholders in the design and dissemination of the research cycle. The position will regularly require interpreting data, highlighting relevant findings, writing engaging briefs and factsheets, presenting findings to external audiences with varying amounts of data literacy, and guiding colleagues in how to think more analytically about their own research.

BACKGROUND OF MULTI SECTORAL NEEDS ASSESSMENT

IMPACT HQ in Geneva support the work of Multi-Sector Needs Assessments (MSNAs) in more than 20 countries. As a result of the World Humanitarian Summit and the Grand Bargain, a commitment was made to “impartial, unbiased, comprehensive, context sensitive, timely and up to date” joint needs assessments that can serve as “a sound evidence base for humanitarian response plans”. These exercises have been informing consolidated humanitarian appeals since 2016. Since 2016, the number of MSNAs supported by REACH has more than quadrupled; MSNA data continues to influence flagship humanitarian response processes such as Humanitarian Needs and Response Plans (HNRPs). This indicates that evidence-based decision making is increasingly becoming a cornerstone of effective humanitarian action.

## **RESPONSIBILITIES**

The Senior Research Officer is responsibilities include:

***Research CYCLE MANAGEMENT***

- Anticipate knowledge gaps prior to the execution of a Research Cycle through strong understanding of the Somali context.
- Ensure that required secondary data review and/or analysis has been conducted in preparation of an assessment.
- Ensure that all research cycles are planned in line with the country strategy, relevant research and project objectives and with IMPACT’s research cycle and other relevant guidelines.
- Design research approaches and methodologies according to IMPACT’s requirements and principles as well as partners’ information needs.
- Compose and construct, in close coordination with GIS and data teams, qualitative and quantitative data collection tool.
- Ensure relevant stakeholders and partners are engaged in research design and planning.

***STAFF MANAGEMENT AND TRAINING***

- Line manage the MSNA Research Officer directly and lead the MSNA team throughout the research cycle
- In close liaison with the Field Manager and Ops teams (field officer and logistics team), manage assessment logistics, including with partner organizations, identifying assessment areas, facilitating design workshops, managing joint data collection processes, and facilitating joint analysis workshops.
- In close liaison the Ops teams, ensure logistics, financial, administration, security and HR processes directly related to ongoing and upcoming assessments are appropriately planned, implemented and coordinated with the relevant Acted departments.
- In close liaison with data colleagues, provide quantitative, qualitative, and spatial data analysis on primary and/or secondary data as per ToRs, ensuring that meaningful techniques are used to analyze the data collected.
- Promoting capacity building across the IMPACT Somalia mission related to deepening analytical capacities using existing research (capacity building portfolio will depend on level of experience)
- Providing day-to-day direct and indirect management of the research team within their unit/workstream, and field team during data collection.
    
    ***Internal Coordination***
- Interacting autonomously with HQ departments and serve as mission focal point for HQ’s corresponding unit and specialists in particular themes or technical areas.
- Engage in the development and implementation of IMPACT’s strategy in Somalia
- Conduct regular meetings with relevant national and international assessment staff members to assess progress in relevant research cycles and to review work plan.
- For all activities, ensure that all assessment and field teams are comprehensively briefed on objectives, expected outputs and that the overall implementation strategy is clearly understood.
- Ensure that project/field staff are given required training and resources to achieve their tasks in line with IMPACT and project requirements. Support to the line managers and specialists in the development and implementation of capacity training plans for team members.
- Be available to provide regular support and technical backstopping; regularly debrief team members to receive feedback on the progress of an activity.
- In coordination with line manager, contribute to conduct induction for new staff members, including training in basic technical competencies for research design, implementation and analysis.

***DISSEMINATION MANAGEMENT***

- Ensure the drafting of timely and accurate outputs that consolidate the analyses from each research cycle into relevant products such as factsheets, reports, briefs, presentations, etc which comply with IMPACT’s guidelines and quality standards.
- Ensure that products accurately reflect the information collected and that information is conveyed in a way that maximizes their impact in line with their intended use for the relevant audiences.
- Follow the designated timeline of reports to be submitted to project partners and donors. Ensure that delays or identified challenges for specific assessments are reported in writing and orally in a timely manner.
- Maintain regular communication with country Management and IMPACT HQ on progress and deadlines for deliverables
- Ensure that all written products are validated by IMPACT HQ before external release.

***External Engagement***

- Ensure that relevant partners are consulted and involved at all stages of research cycle: assessment preparation; data collection; data analysis; review of research products; product dissemination; and lessons learnt.
- After validation by the line manager, represent IMPACT in relevant external meetings/ working groups.
- Follow up on issues identified by partners or during meetings / working groups.
- Promote an active use of datasets and research findings by partners and the broader humanitarian community for their decision making.
- After validation by line manager, disseminate research findings to relevant third parties in order to enhance their use and impact.
- Ensure that all partner engagement and all external relations are clearly documented and communicated with the line manager and relevant colleagues.
- More generally, contribute to the creation of a positive image and overall credibility of the organization, notably through the application of IMPACT’s mandate, ethics, values and stand-point with regard to other actors.

***Data Confidentiality and Protection***

- The Senior Research Officer will maintain the strictest confidentiality on all data collected and related processes, ensuring full compliance with IMPACT’s data protection policy and SOPs. He/she will actively take measures to prevent the unauthorized sharing of any information and data belonging to IMPACT and its partners or collected during his/her assignment with IMPACT.

## **REQUIREMENTS**

- **Research skills** Excellent quantitative and qualitative research data analysis experience required. Ability to adapt, implement and interpret methodology, sampling and analysis to a high standard

- **Thematic experience** Prior experience with MSNA type of research and humanitarian assessments is an asset. Prior experience working with components of FSL/public health is highly desirable

A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.
