title: Humanitarian Access, Safety and Security Advisor
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***Fluency in both written & Spoken French & English required***

Responding to the world’s worst humanitarian crises in a great variety of roles, the International Rescue Committee’s staff is a force for humanity and hope. If you’re skilled and passionate, we’d like to add your energy to ours.

Through its Emergency Unit (EmU), the IRC is one of the world’s largest humanitarian agencies, leading rapid emergency responses that provide life-saving assistance, early recovery, and stabilization support to people affected by conflict, displacement, natural disasters, and complex emergencies across multiple contexts worldwide. We are committed to innovation, agility, and strong partnerships to deliver timely and effective humanitarian action. Active in public health, education in emergencies, livelihoods, women's empowerment, youth development, and protection and promotion of rights, we assist people from harm to home.

The IRC recognizes that people affected by crisis and the actors closest to them are best placed, have the right, and should have the power and resources to respond and drive lasting change. We commit to increasing the share of funding channeled to local actors in emergencies, asking “Why not partner?’ whenever we plan programming, and partner as equals.

**Job Overview:**

IRC’s Global Crisis Analysis, Humanitarian Access, Safety and Security, and Preparedness teams have come together to form ‘ASAP’ (Analysis, Security, Access and Preparedness) to strengthen global and regional support to IRC teams to deliver in the most complex, volatile and high-risk operating environments to reach the worst-affected and least-served people in need. Housed within the IRC’s Emergency Unit, but supporting countries and emergencies responses across IRC’s footprint, the Advisor allies with country and emergency response leadership, ASAP colleagues, and Regional Safety and Security Directors, to provide strategic, technical and operational support to enable IRC to open, expand, and sustain programs in emergencies, major crises, and complex environments – to reach the worst-affected and least-served populations.

The Advisor will work alongside the Director, and the Emergency Response Team Humanitarian Access, Safety and Security Coordinator, to split responsibilities by country portfolio and/or thematic demands and/or level of complexity based on their respective scope of work and experience. The role brings additional capacity, and challenges and supports teams to meet IRC’s mandate through effective analysis and scenario planning to inform program and operational ambitions, and support to deliver on these with enhanced humanitarian access and security management.

The International Rescue Committee’s Emergency Unit (EmU) leads IRC’s global emergency preparedness and response to sudden-onset crises, complex emergencies, and high-risk contexts. EmU strengthens IRC’s ability to operate safely and effectively in volatile environments through surge capacity, systems development, and expert technical leadership.

***Location:** This position is open to national candidates or candidates who have residency in either Kenya, UK or Geneva. Candidates from any other country that has an IRC Office, are welcome to apply as well and will be hosted in that country.*

***Fluency in both written & Spoken French & English required***

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Humanitarian access management**

- Plan and deliver inclusive in-person and remote scenario development workshops as part of wider ASAP support to frontline program teams responding to major crises, linking those scenarios relevant strategies to support the IRC to serve the worst-affected and least-served populations despite conflict, volatility and risk.
- Support frontline program teams to develop and track indicators for tracking crisis developments in support countries, where requested as part of wider support, and actively contribute to information sharing with IRC colleagues about key crisis developments in support countries.
- Support country leadership to develop and implement specific access and acceptance strategies, in support of the Country Director/Emergency Team Leader, ASAP and/or RSSDs to enable and safeguard principled, secure, and sustained humanitarian access to reach target populations, in line with IRC policy and international humanitarian law – these may include a wide range of access approaches including broader risk management and remote management.
- Ensure strategies include how IRC builds relationships, engages and negotiates with authorities, key power brokers, security actors, and community stakeholders, including with state and non‑state actors, to ensure IRC’s mission and activities are understood and accepted, and that staff and programs can operate safely and without disruption.
- Build and maintain an active network of humanitarian access and security staff internally and across organisations.
- Maintain currency with methods, approaches and professional developments in relevant topics, and represent IRC in relevant global fora where needed.

**Safety and security management**

- Support country leadership and access, safety and security teams to identify, analyze and mitigate safety and security (S&S) risks across emergency responses, ensuring alignment with IRC Security Minimum Standards (SMS), Duty of Care, GEDI and PEERS principles, and integrate into access, security, preparedness strategies where relevant.
- Support the implementation of S&S standards and approaches to strengthen humanitarian access, and ensure S&S preparedness and contingency align with program ambitions.
- Support country/response teams in incident management, where relevant.

**Emergency preparedness**

- In close collaboration with ASAP and the Director, Emergency Performance and Quality, support country programs to develop and implement humanitarian access, safety and security approaches in their emergency preparedness and contingency plans, streamlining existing strategies and plans where relevant/possible, through in-country or remote mentoring, training and technical support.
- Support EmU in the development and adaptation of humanitarian access, safety and security systems, practices and resources, and centralized knowledge management.

**Learning & Development**

- Co-develop, with consortium partners, a humanitarian access framework that is accessible and used by partners to define access ambitions and strategies.
- Support the development, revision and uptake of IRC’s technical resources for analysis, security, access and preparedness, learning from operational experience, as well as global trends and good practices.
- Guide, train, coach and mentor IRC country leaders and frontline staff on humanitarian access approaches, safety and security, including Security Risk Management (SRM), and partner capacity strengthening, ensuring the inclusion of gender-sensitive approaches that address gender-specific risks.
- Design, deliver and track humanitarian access, safety and security capacity strengthening activities (including training, coaching, peer-to-peer learning) for EmU and priority country teams in access, safety and security training (including READI and humanitarian negotiation) and context analysis and scenario planning – leveraging internal and external resources.
- Ensure an ongoing exchange of learning and good practice in ASAP methods and approaches with partners; and deliver capacity sharing activities on analysis, access and security where relevant and prioritized.
- Contribute humanitarian access, safety and security content to EmU trainings and conferences and support cross-learning, and to global Safety and Security resources, as relevant.

**Partnerships**

- Champion a culture of effective and respective partnerships across the EmU, including supporting country and emergency teams to provide technical or operational support to partners.
- To further IRC’s partnership ambitions, ensure partners play a central role in the development of access, security and engagement strategies, and the identified approaches, including capacity sharing initiatives.
- Working with the EmU Partnerships focal points, ensure IRC technical resources for humanitarian access, safety and security are adapted and/or oriented towards partners for their own adaptations, and support partners in their uptake and cross-contextual learning and application amongst partners and IR.
- Design and deliver capacity sharing activities with partners where this is identified by the country program and ASAP access and security support, including peer-to-peer exchange and humanitarian negotiation.
- Collaborate closely with consortium partners to learn, coordinate and ensure the shared delivery of each organisation’s analysis, security, access and preparedness approaches within the defined Project results, including grant reporting and capturing case studies.

**Team Culture**

- Build and maintain strong working relationships across EmU, the Global S&S Department and regional/country colleagues to promote a culture of partnership, collaboration and One IRC.
- Cultivate and maintain a positive, collaborative, safe and protective work environment, while additionally setting an example of ‘One IRC’-way of working within the team, EmU, and the wider organization.
- Contribute to efforts across EmU and through ASAP support to safe, diverse, and inclusive culture and ways of working across our programming.
- Foster ongoing learning, honest dialogue, and reflection to strengthen safeguarding, GEDI commitments, and IRC values.

**REQUIREMENTS:**  
**Work Experience:**

- At least 8 years of non-profit or NGO work experience within international humanitarian assistance programs with demonstrated successes in planning, organizing and managing safety and security in complex and volatile environments.
- Significant practical experience in humanitarian access, humanitarian negotiation, civil-military coordination, security management or related competencies.
- Substantial and documented prior experience as a facilitator – the ability to develop, implement, facilitate and impart learning to a wide range of audiences.
- Experience with collaborative/inclusive development of tools, guidance and learning materials for/with practitioners.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- Knowledge of legal and normative frameworks for humanitarian action and expertise in applying humanitarian principles in practice.
- Thorough familiarity with principles and current approaches to humanitarian access and acceptance models of security management, including demonstrated understanding and successes in gender security management and gender equality.
- Ability to gain a precise understanding of the various local, regional, country and international policies, operational positions and interactions, and ability to support analysis and its uptake into decision making before and during emergencies and major crises.
- Advanced skills in humanitarian negotiation, humanitarian-military relations and/or engagement with armed groups.
- Strong communication, diplomatic, relationship building and interpersonal skills, including to influence and obtain cooperation of individuals not under supervisory control.
- Proficiency in facilitating challenging conversations, and challenge teams, on strategic, technical and operational subject matter to create shared understanding and inform decisions.
- Proficiency in delivering training and coaching support to individuals, teams and/or partners.
- Humility in analysis, ways of working and willingness to learn with teams in the most complex settings.
- Able to work as member of multinational team and manage a variety of external and internal relationships to achieve results.
- Excellent ability to produce user-centered, effective, and responsive guidance, tools and materials.
- Ability to summarize sophisticated topics and information inclusively, clearly and succinctly.
- Demonstrated commitment to gender equality, diversity, and inclusion in humanitarian settings.
- Ability to identify and address barriers to inclusion for marginalized and underrepresented groups in emergency response.
- Experience working with diverse teams and communities, including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other groups at risk of exclusion.
- Commitment to ongoing learning and reflection on personal and organizational biases, and willingness to adapt practices to promote inclusion.

**Language Skills:** Proficiency in English and French required; Arabic and Spanish of additional added value.

**Key working relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Director of Emergency Humanitarian Access, Safety and Security

**Position directly supervises:** N/A

**Other Internal and/or external contacts:** ASAP colleagues, Regional Safety and Security Directors, Emergency Safety & Security Coordinator

**Working Environment*****:*** Up to 40% international travel may be required, including to environments affected by armed conflict.

**Compensation:** (Switzerland Pay Rate: CHF 100,000 - 115,000/yr; UK Pay Rate: GBP 60,000 - 66,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Emergency Response Team Supply Chain Coordinator
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***Fluency in both written & Spoken French & English required***

**Role Bakground:**

Responding to the world’s worst humanitarian crises in a great variety of roles, the International Rescue Committee’s staff is a force for humanity and hope. If you are skilled and passionate, we would like to add your energy to ours. Through its Emergency Unit (EmU), the IRC is one of the world’s largest humanitarian agencies leading rapid emergency responses that provide life-saving assistance, early recovery, and stabilization support to people affected by conflict, displacement, natural disasters, and complex emergencies across multiple contexts worldwide. We are committed to innovation, agility, and strong partnerships to deliver timely and effective humanitarian action.

Active in public health, education in emergencies, livelihoods, women's empowerment, youth development, and protection and promotion of rights, we assist people from harm to home. The IRC recognizes that people affected by crisis and the actors closest to them are best placed, have the right, and should have the power and resources to respond and drive lasting change. We commit to increasing the share of funding channeled to local actors in emergencies, asking “Why not partner?’ whenever we plan programming, and partner as equals.

None of this work would reach clients without a supply chain that can keep pace with a crisis. The IRC's Global Supply Chain (GSC) team makes that possible, providing supply chain support to every IRC office worldwide. GSC specialists design and deliver supply chain activities that keep programs moving, in line with internal policy and donor requirements, so that life-saving assistance reaches people affected by conflict, displacement, and disaster without delay.

**Fluency in both written & spoken French Required.**

**Scope of work**

The Emergency Response Team is a specialized group within the Emergency Unit, and members are deployed to either support existing country programs in their emergency response or to initiate a new program in the crisis zone. The overall responsibility of the team is to rapidly and effectively design, develop and manage the IRC’s on-site humanitarian response to meet the immediate needs of the affected population. The ERT is also responsible for supporting the transfer of responsibilities and knowledge to the long-term staff to ensure the continuity of IRC programming and operations. All IRC ERT staff are expected to be deployed in the field, either in an emergency or roving capacity, for up to 65% of the time and must be able to deploy to the site of an emergency within 72 hours of notification.

The IRC ERT Supply Chain Coordinator provides leadership and direction to ensure an effective, high-quality, and timely emergency supply chain response, coordinating across components such as procurement, warehousing and inventory, fleet and logistics, and medical/pharmaceutical supply chains in emergency and outbreak responses, and is a member of both the IRC's Global Supply Chain and the Emergency Unit. The ERT SC Coordinator reports to the Director, Emergency and Health Supply Chain on an ongoing basis and during periods of non-deployment. During emergency deployments, ERT staff work under the direction of IRC's Emergency Response Director or the designated country/regional emergency lead, with technical backstopping provided by the Director, Emergency and Health Supply Chain in the Emergency Unit.

**Major Responsibilities**

**Leadership**

- Provide technical oversight of all Supply Chain functions for emergency response.
- Ensure that processes follow IRC GSC standard operating procedures in all aspects as followed.
- Contribute to field leadership, EmU SAP IP and GSCs strategic workplans,
- Be a voice for the supply chain team within the unit.
- Where applicable s/he will be sent to existing programs to gap fill or provide extra capacity to in country teams
- Be a Subject matter expert (SME) in IRCs ERP, Integra, training and mentoring supply chain and program staff

**Planning**

- Proactively participate in Project Cycle Meetings, including project design, project planning, project opening, project review, project close-out and project learning meetings to ensure that supply chain related issues are well articulated to all stakeholders and resolved for successful project delivery.
- Prepare and maintain emergency procurement plans and develop/maintain country program sourcing strategy for all active and pipeline grants in collaboration with program Technical Coordinators and Managers,
- Ensure that supply chain department is well staffed and roles and responsibilities of each have clear job description.

**Procurement**

Ensure:

- Compliance to IRC and donor policies for all goods and services procurement (including pharmaceuticals and medical equipment)
- In collaboration with the in-country GSC team(s) review and utilize the Procurement contracts (MPA, MSA) in place for the purchases of goods and services.
- The implementation of GSC procurement and contracting SOPs.
- The accuracy of GSC data collected; timely submission of required report(s) to advise the decision-making process.
- Disseminate through trainings the existing procurement process as well the procurement tools to all EmU GSC team members.
- Ensuring all required procurement documents are included in waivers request files (Purchase Requests, Market Surveys Proforma (3), ATC etc.)
- Management of all waivers with details of the emergency procurement circumstances, including the country program leadership approval (CD, DDO) before its approval by either the RSCD or the CGSCO.
- The suppliers’ files prepared by the procurement team are historically documenting the supplier(s) performance feedback provided by the EmU services requesters after the goods/services deliveries.
- The existence of segregations of duties in the procurement functions during the emergency deployment.
- The program requirements for supplies of items and services are timely met.
- The Grant (s) procurement and distribution plans are developed, regularly reviewed and all related issues are timely resolved or raised in collaboration with leadership.
- The end-to-end procurement processes are conducted through IRCs ERP System, Integra
- Any IRC procurement process deviations are identified, documented, and timely reported following the approved mechanism.
- Follow the Pharmaceutical Quality Assurance Policy in procurement and delivery of medical commodities.

**Inventory, Warehousing, Assets and Property**

- The implementation of the IRC inventory policies during the emergency support for all Project Items (cycle count, reporting discrepancies, pharmaceutical quality assurance as well as cold chain policies where applicable).
- The grant inventory report is accurate, regularly produced, reviewed, and approved before the Grant closing date.
- The warehousing safety and security requirements are in place.
- The assets maintenance plans are in place as per IRC policies.

**Fleet and Logistics**

- The vehicle safety policies are in place, disseminated and followed by all vehicles users.
- Effective fuel consumption management tools are developed and in use.
- The fleet legal status (registration, licenses, insurance) are updated;
- The vehicle monthly reports are regularly issued, reviewed and used to inform the leadership strategic decision-making process.
- The vehicle movement planning and tracking tool(s) are in place;
- The driver management policy is developed and followed.

**Learning and Development**

- Every new starter in the SC team receives 90-day objectives
- Accurate staff development plans are developed based on the documented training needs assessment process, discussed with the unit leadership, approved and implemented.
- Each team members' objectives are set following the organizational unit visions as well as operations context(s);
- Ensure all SC staff are trained to standard and sign the IRC code of conduct, conflict of interest following the SOPs recommendations.
- Ensure all counterparts who deal with supply chain processes are trained to standard.

**Compliance and Ethics**

- Identifies and sets mitigation plan to handle Supply Chain risks, including identification of red flags, and implementing internal and external audit corrective action plans to ensure all supply chain activities are conducted in an ethical manner.
- Ensures compliance to IRC and donor policies in the procurement and distribution of program supplies and assets.
- Ensure that assessments of supply chain policies, procedures, controls, and performance is conducted and any deviations addressed in the country program where designated
- Take lead in donor and IRC Internal Audit process of the SC department, develop and support implementation of post-audit corrective action plans and other improvement plans

**Emergency Preparedness**

- Work with the Emergency Unit and high risks country programs to implement emergency preparedness through in country training, mentoring and remote technical support.
- Participate in, and contribute to content for Emergency Unit trainings and conferences

**Partnerships:**

- Champion a culture of effective and respectful partnerships. Promote partner-led programming in line with IRC’s “why not partner?” and “partner as equals” approach
- Actively contribute to the relevant sections of Partner Capacity Analysis (PCA) and the subsequent development of partner support plans
- Be deliberate and intentional in determining whether a partner was capable of key supply chain activities in emergencies or whether IRC needed to take the lead
- Manage the implementation of action items in the Supply Chain sections of partner support plans
- Work collaboratively with partners to ensure that project budgets reflect fair market value
- Ensure appropriate budget allocation for IRC to support partners in alignment with the overall response/program design
- Actively participate in the Partnership Working Group (PWG) if applicable

**Key working relationships**

**Position Reports to:** Director, Emergency Supply & Health Supply Chain (while not deployed),

**Position directly supervises**: On deployment only

**Works closely with:** Other ERT and GSC staff, country program supply chain and management team.

**Indirect Reporting:** Emergency Team Leader/Country Director (while deployed)

**Requirements**

- Advanced Degree, 3-6 years or more of progressive Supply Chain professional experience or equivalent education and experience
- Proven experience developing and managing supply chain/logistics functions in an INGO, including in emergency/conflict areas
- Demonstrated success as a Supply Chain leader across all disciplines including planning, procurement and logistics.
- Demonstrable knowledge and experience in medical logistics and the procurement, storage, transport and distribution of pharmaceuticals
- Broad knowledge and experience in Supply Chain strategies, market analysis techniques, procurement and contracting, vehicle and fleet management, inventory, property and asset management
- Demonstrated skills in building strong teams and establishing new operations, including strong ability to communicate and work effectively with senior management, operating and program staff and functions
- Proven leadership of multi-disciplinary, cross-cultural teams, with strong mentoring, coaching, motivational, and team-building skills
- Demonstrated commitment to inclusion and fair treatment of staff, and ability to identify and address barriers to inclusion for marginalized groups in emergency response
- Strong collaborator and influencer with effective interpersonal and analytical skills who is able to work seamlessly across countries, cultures, and organizational units
- Proven experience in remote management
- Strong financial management and budgeting skills
- Strong computer, radio and communication equipment skills, and licensed and able to drive manual transmission, 4WD vehicles
- Resilient, organized, hard-working, with positive attitude
- Bilingual English and French mandatory; Arabic and Spanish advantageous

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

  
**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Sudan - Head of Programmes
HEAD Of Middle East Durable Solutions Platform
body:
The Danish Refugee Council assists refugees and internally displaced persons across the globe: we provide emergency aid, fight for their rights, and strengthen their opportunity for a brighter future. We work in conflict-affected areas, along the displacement routes, and in the countries where refugees settle. In cooperation with local communities, we strive for responsible and sustainable solutions. We work toward successful integration and – whenever possible – for the fulfilment of the wish to return home.

The Danish Refugee Council was founded in Denmark in 1956, and has since grown to become an international humanitarian organization with more than 7,000 staff and 8,000 volunteers. Our vision is a dignified life for all displaced.

All of our efforts are based on our value compass: humanity, respect, independence and neutrality, participation.

DRC hosts the Middle East Durable Solutions Platform (ME DSP), a membership-based NGO platform established by DRC, NRC and IRC and later joined by Oxfam, ACF and Save the Children to strengthen evidence, programming and advocacy on solutions to displacement in and from Syria. In 2022 its scope was widened to Iraq and Yemen. Following a period of hibernation since 2023, ME DSP has secured core donor funding and is in the process of re-establishing its membership, reviewing its governance and operating model, and diversify its partnerships. ME DSP is one of three DRC-hosted solutions platforms, alongside ReDSS (East Africa and Great Lakes) and ADSP (Asia), and sits within the DRC Middle East, Asia and Europe Hub under the leadership of the Hub’s Executive Director.

The **Head of ME DSP** provides overall leadership, strategic direction and management of the Platform, a membership-based, consensus-driven platform of NGOs working on solutions to displacement across the Middle East. As the Platform’s principal convener, s/he leads engagement with members and governance structures, builds consensus around shared priorities and ensures delivery of agreed commitments; leads the Platform’s evidence, learning and policy agenda so that research is translated into programming and policy guidance; represents the Platform at senior level with members, governments and donors, UN agencies and policy makers at country regional and global levels; manages ME DSP grants, staff and consultants; and works in close collaboration with DRC’s sister platforms, ReDSS and ADSP.

**Responsibilities:**

**Strategic Leadership, Governance and Management**

- Facilitate the implementation of the ME DSP Strategy 2026-2028, lead the regular review of the Platform’s work plans, and ensure ME DSP maintains a strategic, neutral and member-driven role that complements existing coordination mechanisms
- Lead the re-establishment of the Platform’s membership and the review of its governance and operating model, in line with Steering Committee decisions
- Lead annual planning and budgeting and report to the Steering Committee and members on progress, risks and results; maintain the risk matrix, commission periodic evaluation of ME DSP and integrate lessons learned
- Work in close collaboration with ReDSS and ADSP to share learning, align approaches and tools, and contribute to joint NGO engagement in global solutions fora
- Accountable for people management of direct reports, including recruitment, objective setting, performance management and staff development, and for the management of ME DSP consultants

**Membership Convening and Coordination**

- Act as the Platform’s principal convener. Design and facilitate member meetings, technical working groups and consultations in an inclusive and transparent manner that builds collective ownership of the Platform’s agenda and outputs
- Facilitate consensus-building among members, managing differing priorities and resolving issues that may affect Platform decisions and delivery
- Ensure effective coordination and information sharing among members and the Steering Committee, and support members’ engagement with the Platform at country, regional and global levels
- Lead a membership engagement strategy, including the onboarding of new members and clarity on members’ roles and contributions.

**Research, Evidence and Learning**

- Define and oversee the Platform’s research and knowledge management agenda with members, initiating and commissioning studies, managing researchers and research institutions, and ensuring methodologically rigorous, research ethics and relevance to programming and policy
- Lead the analysis of regional displacement and solutions data, strategies, policies and legislation; translate evidence into programming and policy guidance, briefing papers and policy briefs; and ensure quality control of all ME DSP publications and monitoring of their uptake
- Facilitate regular technical workshops and learning events and the roll-out of learning tools and training packages, ensuring cross-learning across countries and with global developments in solutions policy and practice
- Promote the meaningful engagement of displacement-affected communities and local civil society in the Platform’s evidence, learning and policy work

**Policy Engagement and External Representation**

- Represent the Platform at senior level with governments and national authorities, donors, UN agencies, international financial institutions, regional bodies and policy makers, building trusted relationships and navigating politically sensitive contexts with discretion and in line with humanitarian principles
- Oversee the development and implementation of the Platform’s policy and advocacy strategy with members, ensuring positions are evidence-based, agreed by members and coordinated with NGO fora and durable solutions working groups in the region
- Support members’ advocacy with governmental and inter-governmental actors and engage proactively in regional and global policy processes on solutions for displacement-affected populations
- Engage research institutions, think tanks and academia, and oversee high-quality external communications reflecting members’ agreed positions

**Business Development and Project Management**

- Manage existing and future grants, including budgets, work plans, monitoring and donor reporting, ensuring timely delivery and compliance with DRC and donor policies, including safeguarding
- Develop and implement a fundraising strategy to ensure financial sustainability, including donor engagement and partnerships, in coordination with the Steering Committee

**About you**

To be successful in this role we expect you to have **Experience and technical competencies** :

- Advanced university degree or equivalent in political science, international relations, humanitarian law, migration, Middle East studies, or related field
- Understanding of the regional displacement dynamics. Excellent understanding of
- At least 8 years' relevant experience, including 5 in people management and substantial experience leading, facilitating or coordinating a membership-based, consensus-driven consortium, network, NGO forum or inter-agency platform
- Expert knowledge of durable solutions to displacement and the relevant international frameworks, with demonstrated experience in complex and contested return and reintegration contexts
- In-depth knowledge of the displacement context of the Middle East, displacement in and from Syria, Iraq and Yemen, and of the political complexities, policy landscape and coordination architecture of the region
- Demonstrated strategic leadership, ability to manage competing priorities, and ensure accountability for results
- Proven experience in grant management, budget oversight and resource mobilization
- Proven experience in leading, conducting or commissioning research, or in working in close collaboration with researchers, and in translating evidence into programming and policy guidance
- Excellent convening, facilitation and networking skills, with the ability to build trust and broker consensus among diverse organizations; outstanding interpersonal and diplomatic skills, political and cultural sensitivity, tact and impartiality
- Excellent analytical and writing skills, with proven experience producing high quality research and policy briefs and presenting complex information in an accessible manner
- Demonstrated commitment to collaborative working across organizations and with sister platforms, ability to work in a multicultural environment, and flexibility, proactive engagement and high tolerance for change, complexity and unpredictability

**In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:**

**Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.

**Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.

**Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.

**Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.

**Demonstrating integrity:** You act in line with DRC’s vision and values.

**Application process**

All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV (no longer than four pages) in English. **Applications sent by email will not be considered.**

*Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and we encourage interested candidates to apply as soon as possible. We reserve the right to close the vacancy before the advertised deadline if a suitable candidate is identified.* “

**Location:** Jordan/Amman with potential travel in the region

**Contract length**: 1 year contract

**Start date;** 1 Jan 2027

**Closing date for applications:** 16-11-2026.

If you have questions or are facing problems with the online application process, please visit [drc.ngo/jobsupport](https://forms-hr.drc.dk/view.php?id=348161).

For further information about the Danish Refugee Council, please consult our website [drc.ngo](https://drc.ngo/).

title: 22323 Project Officer (Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS))
MOZAMBIQUE - DEPUTY COUNTRY DIRECTOR FOR PROGRAMS (M/F) - CABO DELGADO
body:
## ABOUT US

**Desired start date: ASAP**  
**Duration of the mission: 6 months**  
**Location: CABO DELGADO**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## ABOUT THE MISSION

Solidarités International (SI) has been providing life-saving assistance in northern Mozambique since March 2019, initially responding to Cyclone Idai. As the crisis in Cabo Delgado escalated, SI began operations in Mueda in July 2021 and progressively expanded to other northern districts including Nangade, Muidumbe, Palma and, more recently, Mocímboa da Praia. By 2022, SI had established a coordination office in Pemba and operational bases in Mueda and Palma.

Following the closure of the Palma base, SI opened a new base in Mocímboa da Praia in July 2023 to support urgent returnee needs. Today, SI operates from Pemba, Mueda and Mocímboa da Praia, covering not only the northern districts (Mueda, Mocímboa da Praia, Nangade, Muidumbe and Palma) but also additional districts further south, such as Metuge, Chiúre, Mecúfi and Ancuabe.

At the beginning of 2025, major BHA funding cuts forced a significant restructuring, reducing the mission from approximately 140 to around 50 staff and prompting a reorganisation of operations to maintain essential activities. This restructuring coincided with a deterioration of the security situation in Cabo Delgado, with renewed attacks, increased displacement and unpredictable access since mid-2024.

In early 2026, the mission entered a new phase with the confirmation of significant short-term emergency funding, alongside the launch of a major 3-year development-oriented WASH/FSL/Education project in Consortium. This shift requires strengthened programmatic oversight to manage simultaneous emergency and longer-term interventions within a rapidly evolving operational context.

Despite these challenges, SI continues to deliver principled, needs-based assistance across Cabo Delgado with the support of key donors such as ECHO, SDC, CDCS, IFSAN, UNICEF and WFP.

Projects and activities include:

\- Rapid Response Mechanism to shocks (conflict, natural disasters, epidemics): multisectoral WASH / Food / Shelter-NFI assistance through CVA or in-kind distributions

\- WASH: rehabilitation of large water networks, water points construction/rehabilitation, WASH in schools and health facilities, rainwater harvesting systems, sanitation and hygiene promotion

\- FSL: seeds and equipment distributions, support to cooperatives, cash-for-work and income-generating activities

\- Shelter/NFI: mainly emergency shelter and NFI through RRM

Around 50 staff in total across the mission in April 2026, but it will increase in May/June with the new funding.

SI operates 3 bases:

• Pemba (Coordination / Operational Base): 27 staff

• Mueda (Operational Base): 19 staff

• Mocímboa da Praia (Operational Sub-base): 4 staff

• Chiure (Operational Sub-base) to be opened: 6 staff

The DCDP is based in Pemba and covers operations in all bases of SI in Mozambique.

## ABOUT THE JOB

**GENERAL OBJECTIVE:**

The Deputy CD for Programs (DCDP) is responsible for the overall supervision, quality and strategic orientation of Solidarités International programmatic operations and MEAL systems in Cabo Delgado. S/he ensures effective, high-quality and compliant implementation of programmes in line with SI strategy and donor requirements. S/he supervises Program Managers and the MEAL Manager, supports adaptive programming, and works closely with the Area Coordinator and field teams to strengthen coordination, accountability and operational continuity.

**THE MAIN CHALLENGES:**

1- Major mission restructuring following BHA funding cuts in early 2025, with reduced staffing and evolving organisational set-up, followed by a rapid increase of funding in 2026, including short-term emergency grants and a multi-year development project  
2- Short implementation timelines for emergency projects (6 months) requiring strong planning, monitoring and adaptive management  
3- Volatile and unpredictable security context requiring continuous analysis and flexible programming  
4- Multi-base programme (Pemba, Mueda, Mocímboa da Praia, Chiure) with limited resources and high coordination needs  
5- High workload linked to simultaneous project closures, scale-up of emergency response and launch of new projects  
6- Strengthening and maintaining relationships with local authorities and coordination bodies in a sensitive operational environment

**PRIORITIES FOR THE 2/3 FIRST MONTHS:**

1- Ensure structured supervision of ongoing programmes across all bases and also the suppervision of the technicall departments (WASH, FSL, RRM Co, and MEAL)  
2- Strengthen MEAL systems and ensure effective use of monitoring data and accountability mechanisms for programmatic decision-making  
3- Ensure quality closure of ending projects and structured launch of new projects (Apri-May 2026)  
4- Reinforce program compliance with donor requirements and internal procedures  
5- Clarify roles, workflows and coordination mechanisms between Program, MEAL and Support departments  
6- Lead and coordinate proposal development with Project Managers, Technical Coordinators and the Grants Department  
7- Strengthen representation and collaboration with provincial and district authorities, clusters and key partners

**SECURITY CONSTRAINTS:**

Security level 2 in Pemba with limited constraints.

Mueda and Mocímboa da Praia are security level 3, with more restrictions. Movements and activities depend on local conditions and Security Department guidance.

The security situation remains volatile, with unpredictable insurgent attacks and evolving dynamics involving armed actors. Close monitoring of the context is required for daily movement validation. Travel to field bases is mainly via UNHAS flights.

## YOUR PROFILE

**DIPLOMA AND EXPERIENCE:**

Diploma : Master in humanitarian action, development, international law or any other technical area related to the humanitarian sector

Experience in the humanitarian sector : 3/4 years

Experience on a similar position : 3/4 years

**SKILLS:**

TECHNICAL SKILLS

1. Strong Project Cycle Management skills
2. Solid background or experience in at least one technical
3. Strong understanding of MEAL systems and accountability mechanisms, with ability to ensure effective use of monitoring data for programmatic decision-making
4. Good knowledge of donor compliance and reporting requirements

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS

1. Strong information management capacity and ability to coordinate multiple activities across bases
2. Strong planning, prioritisation and organisational skills
3. Ability to represent SI with authorities, partners and coordination bodies
4. Strong analytical capacity and ability to adapt programming to evolving contexts
5. Capacity to supervise and structure teams in a complex operational environment

**LANGUAGE:**

1. English (mandatory)
2. Portuguese (strong asset)
3. Spanish or Italian (asset)

## SI WILL OFFER YOU...

**A salaried position:**  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 3300 gross per month (3000 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

Pemba is a coastal city with good living conditions for expatriates, including stable water and electricity and reliable 4G internet. There is no curfew, and walking is allowed during the day. SI provides comfortable office and guesthouse facilities close to amenities.

The position is based in Pemba, with frequent visits to the bases. Field bases are reachable by UNHAS flight in less than one hour. Living conditions in field locations are basic but functional.

title: Call for Expression of Interest – Pool of Expertise for Facility 1325
body:
**Project Description**  
As part of the project implemented by Expertise France, the 1325 Facility initiative, we are seeking to expand our pool of gender experts and practitioners in the Women, Peace, and Security agenda in the Syrian Arab Republic.

**Project/Context Description**  
In Syria, more than a decade of armed conflict has led to high levels of widespread violence, massive population displacement, territorial fragmentation, and a severe deterioration of essential public services. In this context, women and girls are disproportionately affected by violence, particularly sexual and gender-based violence, insecurity linked to forced displacement, increased economic precariousness, and the shrinking of civic space. At the same time, despite their central role in community resilience, humanitarian aid, local mediation, and the maintenance of the social fabric, their participation in formal peace, governance, and security processes remains limited, and they are underrepresented in decision-making spaces.  
Thus, in a context marked by still-fragile dynamics of transition and political realignment, as well as significant momentum surrounding prospects for stabilization, issues related to the protection of women’s and girls’ rights and their inclusion in decision-making processes are taking on increased importance. However, these opportunities remain hampered by persistent insecurity, institutional fragmentation, and protection and justice mechanisms, which contribute to maintaining their marginalization in political, security, and humanitarian responses.  
As part of the ongoing political transition in Syria, the transitional authorities have demonstrated a commitment to more inclusive governance and the country’s institutional reconstruction. This commitment, reflected in official statements and certain frameworks supported by the international community, emphasizes the promotion of human rights, national reconciliation, and broader participation by all segments of Syrian society, including women. Efforts have also been announced to strengthen the inclusivity of political processes and consolidate transitional institutions.  
Nevertheless, despite these stated intentions, women’s actual participation in decision-making bodies remains limited, and their representation in governance structures remains marginal. This persistent gap between commitments and concrete implementation highlights the structural challenges facing the transition, in a context where security, institutional, and humanitarian constraints continue to weigh heavily on its trajectory.

The 1325 Facility as a response to these challenges  
In the face of these structural challenges, the implementation of the Women, Peace, and Security agenda remains fragile and insufficient. It is within this context that the 1325 Facility project, implemented by Expertise France and funded by the French Development Agency (AFD), is situated. The 1325 Facility is designed as a flexible and targeted support mechanism aimed at strengthening the implementation of the Women, Peace, and Security agenda in fragile and conflict-affected contexts. The project supports national and local actors—particularly human’s right organizations, public institutions, and civil society partners—through technical and strategic support, capacity building, and the promotion of a more inclusive participation in peace, security, and governance processes.  
Drawing on a human rights-based approach, women’s leadership, and conflict-sensitive analysis, the 1325 Facility aims to contribute to more inclusive, sustainable, and effective responses to conflict prevention, the protection of populations, and peacebuilding in Syria.  
The 1325 Facility aims to support actors working on the Women, Peace, and Security agenda through enhanced technical, strategic, and operational support that is, above all, tailored to local realities. Mobilizing national experts with diverse backgrounds, connections, and experiences is a key lever in implementing this support. The essential requirement is that the mobilized experts possess a mastery of international, regional, and national normative frameworks—tailored to each country—and an in-depth understanding of local, institutional, and community dynamics to ensure maximum impact.  
Approach promoted by the 1325 Facility:  
Through the 1325 Facility, France promotes an ambitious, integrated, and context-sensitive approach aimed at strengthening the effective implementation of the Women, Peace, and Security agenda. This approach is implemented for the benefit of national and local actors, particularly civil society organizations, public institutions, and technical and financial partners. It is based on the following guiding principles:

1. Addressing the structural determinants of gender equality and women’s empowerment in crisis and post-crisis contexts by moving beyond ad hoc responses in favor of sustainable change,
2. Promoting an integrated territorial approach based on a detailed analysis of local dynamics of conflict, power, and gender.
3. Prioritize actions in support of girls and women, while involving boys and men (with a focus on adolescents and young adults)
4. Promote an approach focused on changing behaviors and social norms generally attributed to men and women, power relations, and institutional practices—particularly in terms of representation and at decision-making levels.
5. Sustainably strengthen the capacities of local actors by prioritizing forms of technical support that promote ownership, leadership, and sustainability.
6. Adopt a conflict-sensitive approach that is mindful of the risks of tension, exclusion, or political co-optation, and aims to contribute to the prevention of violence and social cohesion.

**An integrated intervention framework organized by sectoral areas:**

The intervention framework of the 1325 Facility is structured around thematic and sectoral areas that are mobilized in a complementary manner and in accordance with the needs expressed by local actors and national priorities, with the aim of strengthening the key levers of the 1325 Facility agenda. For example, these areas may include governance, peace and security, prevention of and response to sexual and gender-based violence, conflict-related violence, women’s participation and leadership in decision-making processes, particularly peace negotiation mechanisms, as well as strengthening the organizational, administrative, financial, and technical capacities of civil society organizations, particularly those working for women’s rights. They may also include knowledge generation, contextual analysis, and knowledge capitalization to improve the quality and impact of interventions.

Thus, the interventions of the 1325 Facility aim to contribute to:

- Promoting sustainable changes in social and institutional norms by supporting transformative gender approaches tailored to local dynamics.
- Supporting the leadership and organizational development of human’s rights organizations by strengthening their operational and structural capacities, as well as their ability to influence and engage in dialogue with national and international authorities.
- Preventing and responding to conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence by supporting public policies, coordination mechanisms, protection systems, and conflict-sensitive and inclusive community-based approaches
- The provision of sexual and reproductive health services through the maintenance of accessible, high-quality public SRH (sexual and reproductive health) services, as well as by strengthening the capacity of women and adolescent girls to make free, informed, and responsible choices regarding SRH. This capacity is a key factor in their empowerment and in the region’s demographic transition.
- The reduction of all forms of gender-based violence, such as early marriage and pregnancy, violence in schools and hospitals, as well as all forms of violence linked to crises and conflicts.
- Systematically integrate an inclusive approach into peace and security policies, strategies, and programs through gender-based analysis, operational tools, training, and institutional support.
- Inclusive participation in economic, political, and social decision-making bodies through support for quota policies in decision-making bodies and the strengthening of women’s leadership.

Through this approach, the 1325 Facility aims to achieve sustainable outcomes such as:

- greater national and local ownership of the Women, Peace, and Security agenda;
- strengthening the technical and strategic capacities of the actors involved;
- Increasing effective inclusive participation in peace and security processes

**Desired Qualifications**

- At least 7 years of experience in one of the following areas: Women, Peace, and Security; gender equality; prevention of and response to sexual and gender-based violence and/or conflict-related violence; women’s participation in peace, security, and governance processes; or social cohesion in crisis, conflict, or post-conflict contexts, as an individual consultant or trainer;
- Proven experience in supporting the integration of women’s and girls’ rights and the WPS agenda into international cooperation projects, working with the public sector (ministries and decentralized state agencies) and civil society organizations;
- Proven experience in designing and implementing capacity-building and training initiatives for public actors and civil society organizations, particularly those working on women’s rights, on topics related to the WPS agenda. These initiatives may address both WPS-related content and the administrative, financial, and technical capacity-building of the organizations being supported;
- Proven experience in the design, implementation, and monitoring and evaluation of international cooperation projects in fragile or conflict-affected contexts in the Middle East, including Syria;
- Proven ability to coordinate multi-stakeholder activities and represent Expertise France with institutional partners and civil society organizations within the scope of assigned missions.
- Strong writing skills: developing assessments and methodologies, drafting project design and initiation documents;
- Ability to produce practical tools: guides and educational materials, and experience in training trainers.
- Fluency in Arabic (required) and fluency in English or French (at least one of the two languages required) ;
- Knowledge of AFD tools and procedures is an asset;
- Experts must become familiar with the following tools and procedures:
- Tools for analyzing and integrating gender and the FPS agenda
- Gender toolkits produced by AFD
- The “Do No Harm” approach promoted by AFD
- The project cycle according to AFD procedures.

**Additional Information**  
We are primarily seeking Syrian national experts with in-depth knowledge of the local context and, if from the diaspora, who have already carried out missions in Syria. International candidates are not a priority for this mission.  
Experts may be called upon for short-term expert assignments of varying durations (ranging from one week to several months), either in person (primarily in Damascus, depending on access conditions) and/or remotely (working from home), depending on the needs of local partners.  
Please specify your areas of expertise and your availability for travel in your application.

title: Grants Manager Lebanon
body:
**Position**: Grants Manager Lebanon

**Location**: Beirut, Lebanon

**Reporting Relationship**: Country Head of Programmes

**Family Duty Station**: NO

**Starting date**: ASAP

**Application deadline**: 15/11/2026

**Contract Type**: Expatriate (International)

**Working Context**

WeWorld has been working in Lebanon since 2006 and is currently supporting vulnerable refugee, IDP and host community populations through WASH, Food Security and Livelihoods, Local Economic Development, Education and Social Cohesion in Bekaa, Baalbek-Hermel, Akkar, Saida and Beirut. Our interventions span immediate emergency response and recovery in view of building preparedness and longer-term resilience for populations affected by conflict and/or displacement. The operation is run by over 50 employees, divided in three offices (Beirut, Zahle and Saida). We work closely with local partners, including NGOs and institutional actors at different levels, and are part of large consortia with other actors.

**Purpose of the Role**

The **Grants Manager** is responsible for leading and overseeing country-level grants management processes, from funding opportunity identification and proposal development to donor reporting, grant amendments and closeout, ensuring quality, timeliness and compliance with donor requirements and WeWorld procedures.

Reporting to the Country Head of Programmes, the Grants Manager operates with a high degree of autonomy within agreed priorities and delegated authority, while ensuring alignment with the country strategy and internal approval procedures.

The role provides functional coordination to Project Managers and relevant technical and support departments, ensuring clear responsibilities, effective collaboration and timely delivery of grants-related outputs. This coordination does not imply direct line management of Project Managers, who remain responsible for project implementation and the accuracy of their respective contributions.

The Grants Manager is also responsible for strengthening grants management systems, tools and procedures, identifying compliance risks and escalating issues requiring strategic or management decisions to the Country Head of Programmes.

**Main Tasks and Responsibilities**

**Proposal Development and Fundraising**

- Contribute to the development and regular review of the country fundraising strategy with the Country Head of Programmes and Senior Management Team, translating donor mapping, funding trends, programme priorities and pipeline analysis into recommendations on funding opportunities and donor engagement
- Build and maintain a donor database and an updated funding pipeline
- Proactively identify, assess and share opportunities aligned with WeWorld’s strategy and goals in Lebanon
- Lead and own proposal development processes, including grant writing, setting realistic calendars, allocating and agreeing contributions, functionally coordinating Project Managers and other contributors, and consolidating inputs. Be accountable for the quality, coherence, completeness and donor compliance of the final proposal package, ensuring appropriate technical and financial review, internal approval and timely submission. The Country Head of Programmes will provide strategic oversight and approval in line with WeWorld’s procedures
- Ensure learning from implementation and WeWorld’s programmatic strategy are duly taken into account when writing proposals
- Keep WeWorld’s profile up to date and adequately archive all proposal-related documents in WeWorld’s SharePoint files

**Compliance and Reporting**

- Own and regularly update the Grants Tracker and reporting calendar, ensuring clear responsibilities, internal deadlines and visibility of grant obligations, deliverables and compliance risks
- Develop, maintain and oversee the application of guidelines and workflows for proposal development, donor reporting, grant amendments and closeout
- Support the MEAL department and Project Managers with partner due diligence processes and implementation monitoring
- Lead the donor reporting process through functional coordination of Project Managers and relevant departments, setting internal deadlines, consolidating and reviewing inputs, and ensuring consistency between narrative and financial reports. Be accountable for the quality, completeness and donor compliance of report packages and their timely submission following the required internal reviews and approvals
- Provide guidance and build the capacity of Project Managers on grants management, reporting and donor requirements; monitor follow-up on agreed actions and escalate unresolved gaps or delays to the Country Head of Programmes

**Project Cycle Management**

- Coordinate grants-related preparation and follow-up for project kick-off, review and closeout meetings with Project Managers and relevant departments, ensuring grant conditions, reporting obligations, roles and deadlines are understood and tracked, under the strategic oversight of the Country Head of Programmes
- Coordinate guidance on donor compliance throughout implementation, maintain oversight of grants-related risks and corrective actions, and escalate significant issues to the Country Head of Programmes.
- Coordinate routine donor communication on grants matters within delegated authority, seeking approval for commitments or changes requiring management authorization
- Ensure the Project archiving system is up to date: conduct periodic reviews of project documentation, ensuring proper uploading and archiving by the Project Managers
- Coordinate the preparation, review and submission of grant amendment requests with Project Managers and Finance, ensuring their quality and compliance with donor procedures and obtaining the required internal approvals

The duties and responsibilities set forth above are not exhaustive and the role holder may be required to perform additional duties requested by the Line Manager. Proper handover must be ensured before the end of the assignment.

**ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS**

**Qualifications and Knowledge**

- Master’s degree or equivalent in International Cooperation or a related field
- Good computer skills are required
- Knowledge of institutional donor procedures (AICS, EU, AFD, UN)
- Fluency in both written and verbal English is mandatory
- Fluency in both written and verbal Italian is mandatory

**Professional experiences**

- At least 4 years of specific experience in the field of international cooperation
- At least 3 years of specific experience in Grants management
- Proven experience in independently managing proposal development, donor reporting and compliance processes, including coordination of contributions from multiple stakeholders
- Experience working with institutional donors such as AICS, EU, OCHA and UN agencies

**Skills and Abilities**

- Strong grant writing, donor compliance and functional coordination skills, with the ability to independently manage grants processes, coordinate contributors and ensure timely delivery and quality standards
- Excellent organizational and time management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and tight deadlines
- Sound judgement, problem-solving and decision-making skills, including the ability to identify risks and escalate issues requiring management decisions
- Strong leadership, planning and teamwork skills, with the ability to influence and coordinate colleagues across different functions
- Proactive and dynamic attitude
- Ability to adapt and work under constraint, under pressure and in complex and multicultural contexts
- Interpersonal skills and intercultural approach
- Good listening and communication skills
- Good negotiation and conflict resolution skills
- Strong commitment to the Mission of WeWorld, genuine interest in international cooperation development topics
- Demonstrates integrity with regards to NGO values and ethical standards
- Displays cultural, gender, religion, nationality and age sensitivity and adaptability
- Treats all people fairly without favouritism

**Desirable requirements**

- Knowledge of Arabic would be considered an asset
- Previous work experience in Lebanon would be considered an asset

**WHAT WE OFFER**

**Type of contract**: a 6 (six) month contract, renewable subject to funding availability

**Economic conditions**: according to WeWorld Expatriates Compensation Policy Base Salary (2.840€ - 3.440€ monthly) + Contributions reflecting role complexity and hardship level of the duty station + Housing contribution

**Wellbeing & Inclusion**: One day of paid menstrual leave per month. We promote a positive and inclusive work environment based on psychological safety, respect, and team empowerment.

**Flight ticket**: One round-trip air ticket every 12 months of service (between country of residence and duty station)

**Health insurance**: covered

**Family Duty Station**: NO

**R&R**: NO

**Equal Opportunities**

We are dedicated to fostering an inclusive and respectful workplace where everyone has equal access to opportunities. Employment decisions are based on merit, qualifications, and organizational needs, without regard to gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, nationality, religion or belief, age, family or parental status, disability or any other status protected by applicable law.

title: Caseworker
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:**

The Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other ORR qualified immigrants to support a positive integration experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency. The Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Provide comprehensive case management services enrolled clients.
- Conduct intake services with clients to assess needs. Develop self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with each client. Provide individualized support through direct services, referrals, and advocacy.
- Receive referrals for case management for ORR-eligible and TANF-eligible clients and participate in any needed case conference meetings to assure continuity of care.
- Assess client needs, creates Family Self-Sufficiency Plans (FSSPs) and Individual Employability Plans (IEPs), focusing on removing employment barriers, stabilizing, and obtaining and retaining employment.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals, address challenges, and to ensure that available resources are utilized.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in database(s) and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- May train and lead the activities of volunteers and interns.
- Conduct outreach to case management staff, refugee-serving agencies, ethnic community-based organizations, and others to inform service providers and refugees of programs and services.
- Complete eligibility screenings for all referral and enrollment paperwork for all eligible Program participants.
- Provide comprehensive case management services, including assisting with benefits applications as appropriate.
- Guide/assist participants to establish contact and receive support services in the community based on their service plan.
- Ensure all services are linguistically appropriate and help advocate with mainstream service providers for linguistically appropriate services.
- Complete case notes in a detailed and timely fashion.
- Ensure all family data is entered into data management system in a timely manner.
- Assist with the preparation of donor funding reports and new funding proposals.
- Participate in all program meetings, staff development activities, and fully engages as a member of the team.
- Follow all IRC policies, procedures and protocols including adherence to the IRC Way and Child Safeguarding.
- Other related duties as assigned.

**Key Working Relationships:**

- **Position Reports to:**  Casework Supervisor
- **Indirect Reporting:** Interns/Volunteers

**Job Requirements:**

***Education:***

- Undergraduate degree Social Work or similar field strongly preferred; comparable related work experience may be substituted.

***Work Experience:***

- 2+ years of case management experience in a social services environment.
- Experience working with vulnerable or under served populations preferred

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Computer proficiency with an emphasis on Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Teams, Outlook).
- Strong organizational skills and detail-oriented
- Public Speaking and/or presentation experience preferred
- Ability to effectively communicate and work as a team member with collaborative partners, the community, and clients in a cross-cultural, multi-disciplinary environment.
- Ability and willingness to drive 15 passenger van.
- Strong attention to detail with the ability to prioritize and manage time effectively.
- Problem solver capable of working well independently and as a part of a team.

***Language Skills:***

- Proficiency in written and spoken English, bilingual ability preferred in Spanish, Dari, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French or other refugee/immigrant language used in Arizona. Cross-cultural understanding and strong communication skills, both written and verbal.

***Certificates or Licenses:***

- Must have a valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, access to reliable transportation and the ability to travel regularly throughout the service delivery area.
- In accordance with Arizona State Law, must possess or be eligible to receive a fingerprint clearance card.

**Working Environment*****:***

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.
- Must be able to lift 35 to 50 pounds (furniture, household supplies, and food boxes).

**Commitment to Diversity and Inclusivity:** IRC is committed to building a diverse organization and a climate of inclusivity. We strongly encourage applications from candidates who can demonstrate that they can contribute to this goal.

**Compensation:** ($20.97). Compensation is based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.
