title: Senior Nutrition Advisor
body:
All Hands and Hearts is seeking an experienced Senior Nutrition Advisor to lead the design, delivery and quality of its emergency nutrition programming in Gaza. Acute malnutrition among children under five and pregnant and lactating women has risen sharply amid prolonged conflict, displacement and severe restrictions on food access. The successful candidate will provide technical leadership on nutrition across All Hands and Hearts' humanitarian response, ensure programs meet international standards, and represent the organization with the Nutrition Cluster, UN agencies, donors and partner NGOs. The Advisor will also help integrate nutrition into AHAH's wider food distribution, community health, shelter and education programs, and build the capacity of local staff and community health workers.

## Key Responsibilities

- **Technical Leadership:** Serve as AHAH's lead technical expert on nutrition in emergencies, setting program strategy and ensuring all nutrition activities align with Sphere standards, Nutrition Cluster guidance and Ministry of Health protocols.
- **Program Design and Delivery:** Design, launch and oversee nutrition interventions, which may include community-based management of acute malnutrition (CMAM), MUAC screening and referral, supplementary feeding, micronutrient supplementation, and infant and young child feeding in emergencies (IYCF-E).
- **Integration with Food Assistance:** Advise AHAH leadership and logistics teams on the nutritional adequacy of food baskets and distributions, targeting of vulnerable groups, and safe handling of specialized nutrition commodities (RUTF, RUSF, LNS).
- **Assessment and Surveillance:** Lead or support nutrition assessments, screening campaigns and surveillance (including SMART-style surveys where feasible) to identify needs, track trends and guide program decisions.
- **Coordination and Representation:** Represent AHAH in the Nutrition Cluster and relevant working groups; build partnerships with UNICEF, WFP, WHO, health facilities and local NGOs to strengthen referral pathways and avoid duplication.
- **Capacity Building:** Train and mentor AHAH staff, partner organizations and community health workers on nutrition screening, counseling, IYCF-E and the Code on breastmilk substitutes.
- **Monitoring, Reporting and Accountability:** Develop indicators and monitoring tools, ensure quality data collection, and report program results to AHAH leadership and donors. Ensure feedback and accountability mechanisms are in place for affected communities.
- **Resource Mobilization:** Contribute technical content to proposals, budgets and donor reports for institutional and private donors (e.g., USAID/BHA successor mechanisms, ECHO, UN pooled funds, foundations and Gulf donors).

## Qualifications & Experience

- MD or Master's degree in Public Health, Nursing, Nutrition, or a related field.
- Minimum 8–10 years of experience in health or nutrition programming, including at least 5 years in humanitarian or emergency settings.
- Demonstrated technical expertise in nutrition programming.
- Proven experience managing teams, training staff and working through local partners.
- Excellent analytical, communication and representation skills.
- Language requirements: Fluency in Arabic and English (written and spoken).
- Candidates must be willing to undergo a thorough background and security check prior to a final offer. Must demonstrate commitment to neutrality and community service.

## Salary

This is a 18-month, fixed-term contract/consultancy with compensation that will be competitive based on experience and location.

title: Venezuela : Country Finance Manager – Caracas
source: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
body:
**Fixed term | 6 months | ASAP**

## Acted

***Who we are***

Acted works with 19 million people across 43 countries at the intersection of humanitarian, development, climate and environmental programming. We draw on deep contextual knowledge and embrace emerging technologies to save lives, alleviate suffering, and protect and restore our planet. Working in collaboration with a growing ecosystem of local, national and international partners, we pursue one shared objective: a 3Zero World – Zero Exclusion, Zero Carbon and Zero Poverty.

***Who we are looking for***

You bring the core competencies required for classical humanitarian and development work, alongside an active climate and environmental conscience, and you can navigate the challenges that arise when human and environmental suffering intersect. You have an entrepreneurial mindset: you see opportunities, connect dots, adapt your approach to different environments, and take measured risks in pursuit of results. You balance principles with pragmatism, and ambition with humility.

## Acted Colombia - Venezuela

Colombia continues being affected by a complex humanitarian crisis, characterized by multidimensional factors such as protracted armed conflict, natural disasters, and mixed movement/displacement dynamics (both internal and external displacement). Moreover, the crisis is exacerbated by the limited presence of state actors in several zones of the country, especially in hard-to-reach and rural areas combined with high poverty rates (36.6%) and food insecurity levels (30%) resulting in approximately 9.1 million people estimated in need of humanitarian assistance.

In parallel, Venezuela continues facing a severe humanitarian crisis, with nearly 8 million people having migrated since 2014, marking the largest exodus in Latin America. 7.9 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance due to the deterioration of basic public services and a deep economic crisis characterized by high inflation rates and lack of purchase power, resulting in an estimated 56% of its population living in extreme poverty. Moreover, according to the OECD, Venezuela also ranks among the top 3 countries with the highest increase in human fragility, while 40% of the population experience moderate to severe food insecurity and 62% face restriction on access to drinking water. Highly vulnerable communities, living in rural and border areas are affected the most, and 1.4 million children are estimated in need of protections assistance.

## You will be in charge of

The Country Finance Manager (CFM) is a key member of the Management Team at country level. He/she will be responsible for Acted financial management in-country under the authority of the Country Director and Finance & Administrative Director in HQ. The CFM ensures that national legislation is adhered to, and that Acted’s financial standards are applied in terms of accounting, financial control systems, internal / external reporting processes, in order to ensure an efficient use of resources. He/She leads, provides technical support and capacity building to the country finance and administrative staff. The CFM shall alert the Country Director and Finance Director in case some major problems arise with a potential financial impact on the mission.

***Main duties***

1\. Accounting and treasury Management

- *Accounting management – supervise the accounting cycle for the mission*
- *Treasury management – ensure a controlled and smooth cash management*

2\. Commitment of expenditures, budget control, & Financial Management

- *Commitment of expenditure – guaranty budget availability and compliance to Acted and donor’s procedures before releasing payments*
- *Project budget follow-up, mission’s cost control, internal & external audits – anticipate and mitigate financial risks ensuring operations are run in a compliant and cost-efficient manner*

3\. Project financial cycle management

- *Develop project budgets and reports – ensure the financial feasibility of projects, respecting Acted and donors’ rules and deadlines*

4\. Team leadership & other tasks

## Expected skills and qualifications

- Msc in Finance, Audit, Business Management, Economics or equivalent;
- 3+ years of solid experience in financial & budget management;
- Excellent financial and analytical skills;
- Excellent communication and drafting skills for effective reporting on programme financial performance;
- Ability to manage a financial team and demonstrate leadership;
- Ability to monitor and evaluate financial skills of teams through capacity-building efforts;
- Ability to undertake serious responsibilities and to manage stress efficiently;
- Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment requiring flexibility;
- Prior knowledge of the region an asset.

## Conditions

- Salary between 3300 and 3500€ monthly (before income tax), depending on the level of education, security level, etc as well as a monthly living allowance of $300
- Accommodation and food provided in Acted guesthouse
- Pension, health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance (& unemployment insurance for EU citizens)
- Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered
- Contribution to the luggage transportation: up to 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract
- R&R every 3 months, flight tickets covered up to $500 and allowance of $200
- Annual leave of 25 to 43 days per year
- One week pre-departure training in Acted HQ, including a 4-days in situ security training
- Tax advice (free 30-minute call with a tax consultant)
- Psychological assistance
- This position is classified as an **international staff position** under Acted’s recruitment framework. Eligibility for an international contract is therefore required.

The National Virtual Program for Professional Advancement (NVPPA) is a nationwide, fully virtual program through which IRC will serve newly arrived refugees under a cooperative agreement with the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR). Participants receive career navigation, training, job placement support, and direct financial assistance to advance an individualized career goal.

The NVPPA Supervisor manages the day-to-day work of the program's direct service team across a fully virtual, national caseload. - Resolve escalated participant issues in partnership with the Customer Service Representative, and determine when an issue requires the Deputy Director's involvement.
- Support onboarding and ongoing training of direct service staff.
- Translate program requirements into standard operating procedures and desk guides for the direct service team.

**Program quality and compliance**

- Ensure required safeguards are applied to higher-risk uses of financial assistance, such as vehicle purchases.

- Monitor progress against program targets, identify barriers in the service model such as digital access, language access, or credential evaluation delays, and work with the Deputy Director on practical adjustments.

**Coordination**

- Coordinate handoffs among navigation, training, financial assistance, and job placement so that participants move smoothly through the program.

- Experience developing standard operating procedures or workflow documentation, and familiarity with credential evaluation, professional licensing, or recertification pathways, preferred.
- Demonstrated commitment to client confidentiality and data protection, including oversight of how a remote team handles sensitive personal and immigration documents, required.
- Strong problem-solving, prioritization, and time management skills, and demonstrated success working in a multicultural environment.

**SCOPE:**

*“This position has an end date of Month, Day, Year.”*

The Deputy Director, NVPPA provides leadership to the National Virtual Program for Professional Advancement, an Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) funded program implemented in FY27. The Deputy Director leads the NVPPA team and ensures sound program implementation, compliance with ORR regulations, client success, and strong staff supervision and support.

NVPPA is a cooperative agreement carried out over a single 12-month period of performance, September 30, 2026 through September 29, 2027. The Deputy Director is accountable for delivering the program on time, within budget, and in compliance with the terms of the award.

**Major Responsibilities:**

***Program Implementation and Deliverables***

- Lead program start-up so that intake, staffing, data tools, and referral protocols are in place as clients arrive, with interpretation and device support where access is a barrier.
- Set and enforce service standards across a high-volume, light-touch model, including a completed Professional Advancement Plan (PAP) and documented career navigation for every enrolled participant.
- Oversee delivery of training, job development, and placement support, and ensure related records are maintained.

***Grant Compliance and Award Management***

- Ensure the program is implemented in accordance with ORR policy, the terms of the cooperative agreement, applicable federal award regulations and cost principles, and IRC policies on data protection, client confidentiality, and safeguarding.
- In partnership with the Senior Director, serve as the program's primary point of contact with the ORR program officer and coordinate with ORR staff, partners, and technical assistance providers.
- Protect the integrity of program eligibility, ensuring eligibility rules are applied consistently and documentation is collected and retained for every enrolled participant.
- Own the internal control environment for direct financial assistance, including documentation before disbursement, alignment with the participant's approved PAP, vendor and training provider verification, and application of IRC Global Supply Chain protocols.
- Maintain audit-ready documentation and ensure required program and financial reports are accurate and submitted on schedule.
- Identify, escalate, and resolve compliance risks, including suspected fraud, working with IRC finance, compliance, and award management colleagues on corrective action.

***Budget and Financial Oversight***

- With the Finance Manager, manage the program budget, monitor spending, and ensure full and timely spend-down and closeout of the award.
- Where a shortfall is projected, provide revised projections and propose reallocation to additional eligible services or a budget revision, at ORR's direction.

***Data, Performance, and Quality Assurance***

- Ensure Efforts to Outcomes (ETO) is configured to program requirements and serves as the system of record, working with the data team on data quality, reporting, and staff training.
- Monitor performance against outcome targets and use data to identify barriers and adjust the service model.
- Establish and oversee a routine quality assurance cycle covering case files, PAPs, and assistance documentation, with findings tracked to resolution.

***Supervision and Staffing***

- Lead recruitment, hiring, and onboarding of a newly formed, fully remote team, and ensure all staff are trained on eligibility rules, eligible uses of funds, documentation standards, and the database.
- Directly supervise the NVPPA Supervisor and the Customer Service Representative, and manage performance, workload distribution, and professional development, and structure staffing so that direct service capacity can be adjusted as enrollment volume becomes known.

***Coordination and Representation***

- In close collaboration with the Program for Initial Resettlement (PIR), oversee guidance on appropriate co-enrollment with PIR and other ORR programs, such as Matching Grant, so that participants can meet initial self-sufficiency requirements while pursuing career goals.
- Establish referral and coordination protocols with sister resettlement agencies, IRC offices, and other service providers so that eligible clients can access the program regardless of which agency resettled them, and represent the program to IRC office leadership and external partners.

**KEY WORKING RELATIONSHIPS**

**Position reports to:** Senior Director, Economic Empowerment

**Directly supervises:** NVPPA Supervisor; Customer Service Representative

**Indirect supervision:** Direct service team, through the NVPPA Supervisor

**Key relationships:** Internally, the NVPPA team, Economic Empowerment Technical Unit, IRC office leadership, and headquarters finance, compliance, and award management colleagues. Externally, ORR, PIR providers, sister resettlement agencies, training providers, and employers.

**Requirements:**

- University degree in Business, Public Administration, Social Work, Economics, Community Development, or a related field required; comparable work and/or lived experience may be substituted.
- Minimum of 10 years of experience with progressive responsibility in the design, development, and implementation of workforce, employment, or broader economic empowerment programming, including program monitoring and evaluation.
- Minimum of 5 years' experience managing staff, including remote or geographically distributed teams, with demonstrated ability to coach staff and manage performance directly and through supervisors.
- Demonstrated experience managing federally funded awards and their compliance and reporting requirements; ORR or other HHS award experience strongly preferred.
- Demonstrated experience overseeing client-level direct financial assistance or comparable payment processes, with a strong grasp of internal controls, required; experience with audits or funder monitoring preferred.
- Demonstrated ability to launch a program quickly and manage a budget of comparable scale through spend-down.
- Demonstrated understanding of refugee resettlement and employment services in the U.S. context; familiarity with credential evaluation and professional licensing pathways preferred.
- Excellent communication and organizational skills, including a track record of reporting difficult information to funders accurately and on time.
- Microsoft Office Suite required; ETO or comparable client database experience preferred.
- Commitment to anti-racism and ongoing learning, and English fluency, required.

**Working Environment**

Fully remote, U.S.-based position requiring reliable high-speed internet, a private work space suitable for confidential discussions, and scheduling flexibility across U.S. time zones; occasional travel may be required.

**Compensation:** ($94,000 - $105,000 \[GEO 1\]). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403(b) retirement savings plan with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Programme Coordinator - UKRAINE (M/F/X)
body:
**Working environment:**

The humanitarian situation in Ukraine remains critical amid ongoing international conflict. Since the escalation of the armed conflict on 24 February 2022, the destruction of vital civilian infrastructure continues to rise, leading to the destruction of homes across the country and cutting off access to critical services for millions of people. In 2025 in Ukraine, the UN estimates approximately 12.7 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance. Ukrainian refugee numbers abroad stand at about 6,9 million, while 3,7 million people are internally displaced (IDPs) within Ukraine.

The severe damage to critical infrastructure such as hospitals, schools, and water treatment plants has compromised access to clean water, sanitation, and essential healthcare services. Constant and long-lasting disruptions to the power grid have plunged entire regions into darkness, hindering communication and hampering daily life.

With the humanitarian situation in Ukraine being a challenge and may deteriorate further, the International Red Cross & Red Crescent Movement continues mobilising its emergency response mechanisms. Together, ICRC, IFRC, Ukrainian Red Cross Society (URCS) and Partner National Societies (PNSs) are undertaking a coordinated response in contributing to URCS interventions as per One Plan 2023-27 and URCS Strategic Plan 2026-2030.

Reporting to the Head of Delegation, the Programme Coordinator will contribute to the development and implementation of the operational strategy of the Delegation, ensure the effective leadership of the country programme - including design, development, and implementation of the programmatic strategy, and contribute to the representation of the Delegation to partners, humanitarian coordination bodies and other relevant stakeholders.

**Missions:**

- **Strategy Development & Grants Management:** Leads on all aspects of programmatic design and actively develops the strategic & operational positioning as well as the development plan of the FRC UA Delegation, in support of the Head of Delegation. Development and writing of new quality Concept Notes and Project Proposals, in coordination with URCS and in line with the Delegation's annual and multi-annual strategic programming, as validated by FRC and URCS. Leads the monitoring, follow-up and accountability of/on active funding agreements. Follows attentively the “Funding Opportunity Watch” that is shared by FRC HQ; in the context of the transition from non-restricted earmarked funding to back donors-funded resources for the FRC “Ukraine Response”.
- **Projects & Team Leadership and Coordination for “Quality Implementation” Follow-up & Monitoring:** Ensures leadership, effective and dynamic management and good coordination of all projects and programmes, the multi-lateral teams involved (FRC and URCS) and of the interactions with FRC HQ (Desk Manager), to ensure “project implementation & quality” monitoring (working closely with all relevant technical experts and counterparts as well as in constant coordination with URCS); including the adequate support to the URCS Programme & Finance teams in the planning, implementation, monitoring, evaluation and reporting of projects; in line with FRC's international strategy, procedures and MEAL obligations in the country of intervention.
- **“National Society Development” Focus:** in the spirit of contributing to the partner’s sustainable development, participates actively in identifying the needs and priorities of URCS that are matching FRC’s international expertise and potential added-value; in order to develop FRC’s knowledge & understanding of URCS strategy and the NSD reference framework of IFRC and FRC.
- **PMER/MEAL:** Ensures that all of URCS’s monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning processes and tools are in line with FRC requirements and properly activated and implemented; in order to ensure quality reporting and feedback mechanisms to beneficiaries, partners and potential donors.
- **Partnership Management & FRC Representation:** Proactively contributes to good partnership relations and the sustainable capacity building of URCS, including to any further support activities that the position may require; as well as contributes to the representation of FRC operation and interests, in support of the Head of Delegation.

**Managing lines:**

- **Incumbent reporting line**: Reporting to Head of Delegation
- **Incumbent operational links:** HQ Desk Manager
- Incumbent will manage:1 International staff (team under construction):
    - Incumbent will manage and technically support FRC Delegation’s technical programme/project delegates and managers.
    - Number and positions of technical managers is defined by the Delegation’s approved structure and can/will evolve over time.

**Qualifications and experience**

**Experiences :**

- At least 3 years’ experience in the same type of position in Coordination
- Previous experience in programme coordination positions
- Previous experience in supervising staff and supporting their professional and technical development.
- Experience and/or knowledge in communicating with various partners and donors
- Experience in developing new projects (concept note, proposal, budget, logframe, etc)
- Experience in donor reporting and contract management
- Experience working with local partners and partner-implemented projects / programmes
- Experience working with the Red Cross Red Crescent Movement
- Experience in donor reporting and financial contract management (previous experience with French donors is a strong asset: AFD, Expertise France, CDCS.
- Experience in the region and specifically in conflictual context is a strong asset
- Background in health or in health projects (including emergency medical services, nurse sciences, pre-hospital care, first aid, etc.) is a strong asset

**Education :**

- Studies in humanitarian or development project coordination or technical profile
- Mastery of the project cycle and project management tools
- Mastery of the humanitarian coordination system

**Skills**

**Mandatory job requirements**

- Organisational capacity
- Coordination capacity
- Strong writing and synthesis skills (for both proposals and reporting contributions)
- Effective capacity in grant management
- Effective capacity in MEAL procedures and processes
- Strong communication and diplomatic skills in multicultural work environments
- Teamwork skills (active listening, proactivity and consensus building)
- Experience in team management
- Initiative and ability to work efficiently and effectively without close supervision

**Valued skills**

- Proficiency in Office (Word, Excel, Powerpoint), networking (Google-Suite/Google Workspace)
- Expertise in identifying and implementing jointly capacity-improvement plans
- Experience facilitating trainings and accompanying staff to strengthen their expertise
- In-depth knowledge of the Red Cross Red Crescent Movement’s National Society Development approaches, especially through a Programme Coordination and Development lens

**Skills related to the specific environment of the mission:**

- Flexibility and quick adaptability
- Restraint, patience and diplomacy in institutional relations
- Ability to work within a coordination team and in functional link with the project and field teams
- Ability to work with a multicultural team
- Resilience to stress and high workload
- **International driving licence mandatory**

**Languages**

- English mandatory (oral and written);
- French or other language of the region would be an asset

**Conditions of employment:**

- Type of status: expatriate
- Type of contract: Fixed-term contract under French law
- Salary: According to the classification of the position on the CRf grid and the experience of the candidate
- Per diem: daily per diem which varies according to the country
- Leave: 10 to 15 days minimum every 6 months - Airfare paid at 100% by CRF for home travel
- Health coverage: CFE + Mutuelle MSH (covered 100%) - covered at 75% by the CRF
- MedEvac/repatriation insurance: YES
- Other insurances: Provident insurance (death and disability)

**SUMMARY**

- Location: Kyiv (with planned movements in Lviv, Kharkiv and possible other locations) - UKRAINE
- Duration: 12 months renewable
- Starting date: December 2026
- Mandatory driving licence

The French Red Cross reserves the right to close a recruitment before the closing date of the advertisement and the application deadline. Thank you for your understanding.

If we do not contact you within 3 weeks, please consider that we will not consider your application.

Female candidates are encouraged to apply.

**Online training**

To learn more about the Red Cross Movement, we invite you to follow two online training courses, free of charge and accessible to all. W.O.R.C. (World of Red Cross and Red Crescent): this course covers topics such as the origin and history of the Movement, its fundamental principles, the emblem, the International Federation, the ICRC and the national societies. Stay Safe aims to develop a common culture of security management within the Movement. You can find these courses on the International Federation's Learning Platform: [https://ifrc.csod.com/client/ifrc/default.aspx](https://ifrc.csod.com/client/ifrc/default.aspx)

title: Youth Program Supervisor
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**JOB OVERVIEW:**

The Youth Program Supervisor provides leadership and oversight for IRC's youth programming, including program operations, staff supervision, partnerships, compliance, resource development, and strategic planning. This role works collaboratively with staff, schools, families, and community partners to ensure high-quality services and positive outcomes for youth. The position reports to the Youth Education Manager.

 **MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES**

 **Program Design and Management:**

- Lead department and program planning in alignment with organizational mission and goals.
- Ensure high-quality services that empower youth and support their success in the community.
- Research, develop, and implement best practices that promote positive youth development and academic achievement for vulnerable youth.
- Establish and implement annual and long-term goals and objectives in collaboration with department leadership and staff.
- Ensure compliance with all program, donor, contractual, and IRC standards and requirements.
- Oversee accurate and timely financial, programmatic, and client recordkeeping, including use of ETO and ARRPODS systems.

**People Management**

- Supervise, coach, and support the professional growth and development of Youth Program staff.
- Lead training for staff and volunteers on education best practices, positive youth development, social-emotional asset development, and working with English Language Learners (ELLs).

**Resource Development and Partnership Development:**

- Contribute to grant and proposal development efforts to support and sustain programming.
- Develop, maintain, and strengthen relationships with school districts and strategic community partners.
- Represent IRC Youth Programs within the community and to current and prospective funders.
- Serve as a resource for information related to program activities.
- Perform other duties as assigned.

 **JOB REQUIREMENTS:**

- Bachelor's degree required; graduate degree in education, nonprofit management, public administration, social work, human services, or a related field preferred.
- Minimum three years of experience working with youth and two years of supervisory experience; experience with refugee and/or immigrant youth preferred.
- Demonstrated success in designing and implementing youth programs, leading staff, and building community partnerships.
- Strong communication, relationship-building, and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively across diverse cultures, backgrounds, and perspectives, and uphold IRC values.
- Commitment to serving immigrant communities through trauma-informed and culturally responsive practices; bilingual abilities preferred.
- Valid driver's license, access to a personal insured vehicle, and ability to travel regularly throughout the service area.

 **Working Environment:**

A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities. Some evening and weekend hours will be required.  
  
**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $63,296.42/annual). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Field Volunteer – Women's Empowerment & Self-Defense in Athens
body:
## **About EmpowerVan**

[EmpowerVan](http://www.empowervan.org) is a non-profit organization dedicated to empowering women and girls on the move through self-defense and empowerment training. Our mission is to enable them to lead autonomous lives free from violence.

We currently operate programs in refugee camps and shelters for unaccompanied minors in Greece. There, we have a fully furnished van with martial arts equipment, that we drive to refugee camps, in order to teach self-defense to the people living there. We also go to shelters for unaccompanied minors and other spaces in Athens, to empower asylum seekers and refugees.

This year we have expanded our holistic approach to Kenya, bringing empowerment programs directly to women and girls in Kakuma Refugee Camp, where we certified refugees living in the camp as Empowerment Self-Defense Instructors, and men as Male Agents of Change, driving positive change in their community.

**Field Volunteer – Women's Empowerment & Self-Defense in Athens**

EmpowerVan is looking for a woman that is driven to advance gender justice, loves connecting with community members and has a passion for movement and sport. We are a small team and are looking for a volunteer to help us in Athens. You will be supporting us by going to classes in camps and shelters to support our instructors as you assist them, help with attendance, and you will also help us do reach-out to new community members, drive the van (is you have a license) and support us in daily tasks.

**What we’re looking for**

- **Teaching Skills**: Ability to teach sport, self-defense, or martial arts.
- **Gender Requirement**: Female applicants only (due to the nature of our work).
- **Personal Attributes**: Adaptable, well-organized, able to work independently, and at least 22 years old.
- **Experience**: Prior experience in sport and movement (hobby or work), experience working with displaced communities or minorities is preferred but not necessary.
- **Availability**: Able to be on the ground in **Athens for a minimum of 5 weeks**. Preferably afor at least 16 hours per week, up to full-time.
- People with a driver’s license highly preferred
- **Language skills:** Good spoken English is a must, as the team communicates in English.  
    Additional language skills are a huge plus, especially Persian, Arabic and French

## **Important Notes:**

- This is an **unpaid volunteer position**.
- Applicants must be self-sufficient and able to cover their own expenses during the volunteering period.

title: Internship – Women's Empowerment, Self-Defense and Martial Arts in Athens (Women only)
body:
## **About EmpowerVan**

[EmpowerVan](http://www.empowervan.org) is a non-profit organization dedicated to empowering women and girls on the move through self-defense and empowerment training. Our mission is to enable them to lead autonomous lives free from violence.

We currently operate programs in refugee camps and shelters for unaccompanied minors in Greece. There, we have a fully furnished van with martial arts equipment, that we drive to refugee camps, in order to teach self-defense to the people living there. We also go to shelters for unaccompanied minors and other spaces in Athens, to empower asylum seekers and refugees.

This year we have expanded our holistic approach to Kenya, bringing empowerment programs directly to women and girls in Kakuma Refugee Camp, where we certified refugees living in the camp as Empowerment Self-Defense Instructors, and men as Male Agents of Change, driving positive change in their community.

**Field Volunteer – Women's Empowerment & Self-Defense in Athens**

EmpowerVan is looking for a passionate and dedicated woman to join our team as an intern. You will be helping the on the ground **in Athens** and, go to classes with them, assist, help with class attendance, reach-out to new community members as well as both driving the van and teaching classes if you have the skills needed.

**What we’re looking for:**

- **Physical Skills**: We prefer someone who is a sports-person and is interested to learn teaching basics, especially someone who has experience in self-defense or martial arts.
- **Gender Requirement**: Female applicants only (due to the nature of our work).
- **Personal Attributes**: Adaptable, well-organized, able to work independently, and at least 21 years old.
- **Experience**: Prior experience in sport and movement. Working with displaced communities or minorities is preferred.
- **Availability**: Able to be on the ground in **Athens for a minimum of 5 weeks**. Preferably 3-6 months.
- People with a driver’s license highly preferred
- **Language skills:** Good spoken English is a must, as the team communicates in English. Additional language skills are a huge plus, especially Persian, Arabic and French

**Important Notes:**

- This is an **unpaid volunteer position**.
- Applicants must be self-sufficient and able to cover their own expenses during the volunteering period.

If you’re ready to make a meaningful impact and join a dynamic team dedicated to creating a world free of gender-based violence, we’d love to hear from you!

**Job Overview:** The Sr. Economic Empowerment Manager coordinates the development, implementation, and completion of all grants, contracts and activities related to the Economic Empowerment department, including workforce development, small business development, financial capabilities, and career pathways programming. The Sr. Manager provides direct oversight of the Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA) program and the One-Stop Operator program, supervising the RCA Program Manager and the One-Stop Operator Project Manager to ensure both programs are administered in compliance with donor, state, and federal requirements. The Sr. Manager also leads the ongoing development and long-term sustainability of workforce development and career pathways programming. Responsibilities include supervision of department staff to ensure program compliance across all Economic Empowerment programming.

**Responsibilities:** Include, but are not limited to:

**Oversight of Programs:**

- Effectively lead the development, implementation, compliance, and completion of Economic Empowerment grants and contracts.
- Responsible for the development of grant proposals and reports related to all areas of contracts and grants within the department.
- Supervise the provision of services through regular and systematic case file reviews, and quality assurance protocols including data QA to ensure compliance with donor requirements and provision of quality services.
- Lead all aspects of department program budget and manage expenses to ensure costs are maintained within allocated budgets.
- Provide oversight and strategic direction for the Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA) program, supervising the RCA Program Manager to ensure timely, compliant delivery of cash assistance benefits to eligible refugee and new American clients in accordance with Arizona Department of Economic Security (ADES) and federal guidelines.
- Provide oversight and strategic direction for the One-Stop Operator program, supervising the One-Stop Operator Project Manager to ensure integration of workforce development services across system partners and compliance with federal and local workforce standards.
- Lead the development and long-term sustainability of workforce development and career pathways programming, including building new pathways, employer and community partnerships, and funding streams to support program growth.

**Staff Supervision and Other Responsibilities:**

- Directly supervise the RCA Program Manager and the One-Stop Operator Project Manager, in addition to other Economic Empowerment department staff, ensuring each program area is well-led, compliant, and resourced.
- Participate as an active member of the office leadership team and relevant internal and external groups.
- Lead the team members; formally evaluate team and individual performance to ensure objectives have been met.
- Recruit and train staff in all aspects of economic empowerment programs responsibilities.
- Represent IRC in public, professional and governmental forums. Build community partnerships and Lead local outreach to small businesses.
- Facilitate interdepartmental communication and information sharing for monthly newsletters, program reports, etc.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

- University degree (four year, B.A.) required; advanced degree in related field preferred.
- 5+ years of related program management experience including staff management, program development, and monitoring and evaluation.
- Previous fundraising and grant writing experience.
- Experience overseeing multiple concurrent programs and program managers preferred; familiarity with Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA)/ADES requirements and workforce system operations (e.g., WIOA, One-Stop/American Job Center models) is a strong plus.
- Demonstrated ability to promote an organizational culture that reflects IRC’s core values of service, accountability, integrity, and equality. Ability to lead through the true collaboration of individuals from many cultures with a great variety of skills and perspectives.
- Strong analytical and training skills; excellent written and oral communication skills.
- Highly organized self-starter with proven success managing multiple priorities, making critical decisions, and delivering results in a fast-paced environment with tight deadlines.
- Solid diplomacy, relationship building, and networking skills; ability to effectively manage internal and external relationships, including community stakeholders and donors.
- Fluent in English, both spoken and written. Proficiency in a second language is desirable.
- Demonstrated proficiency in working with MS Office applications, with a strong command of Excel.
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.
- Must possess or be eligible to receive an Arizona fingerprint clearance card.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**Compensation:** ($69,939.00 - $92,500.00/annually). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: ETHIOPIA - FIELD COORDINATOR (M/F) - TIGRAY
body:
**Desired start date: 01/12/2026**  
**Duration of the mission: 6 Months**  
**Location: Adwa - Tigray Region**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

PRESENTATION OF THE MISSION:

Solidarités International (SI) was registered in Ethiopia in December 2022, having previously implemented a WASH in Health intervention in Jijiga, Somali Region, in 2017. In November 2023, SI became the first humanitarian actor to operate in Mao Komo Special woreda (Benishangul-Gumuz) by rehabilitating water points in areas that had been inaccessible for three years. Currently, SI is operational in two regions of the country (In Tigray Region and Amhara Region).

In Tigray, bordering Eritrea, focusing on hard-to-reach areas in partnership with Mums for Mums (MfM) SI is implementing an emergency multisectoral humanitarian programme in Ahsea and Rama Woredas of central zone, to support communities affected by drought, conflict, and displacement. Running from September 2024 to December 2025 (which is now to be extended until end of June 2026), the project aims to improve access to safe water, health services, and nutrition support, while addressing gender-based violence and mental health needs. Key activities include rehabilitating water systems and health facilities, community-based malnutrition screening, cash assistance for vulnerable households, and capacity-building for local actors.

In Amhara region, Solidarités International (SI) and Première Urgence Internationale (PUI) are jointly implementing an integrated emergency response program in the Amhara region of Ethiopia, primarily focused on Health and Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) services. This program is part of a wider effort to address the significant humanitarian needs in the region caused by ongoing conflict and displacement.

SI has been granted cost extension (the donor contract is extended until end of June 2026 with additional fund allocation) of existing project in Tigray and is looking for a Field Coordinator to continue the project activities in the same area.

GENERAL OBJECTIVES :

The Field Coordinator is the representative of the organization at field level. He/she proposes a strategy for his/her area, according to the geopolitical and humanitarian context, and ensures its implementation once validated. He/she checks and ensures that projects are carried out in accordance with the Solidarités International charter, respecting all internal and contractual procedures. He/she mobilizes the material and financial resources necessary for programs to run smoothly and supervises resource management. He/she coordinates the teams in place and is responsible for their security in his/her assigned zone.  
Representation and Internal / external communication:  
The FC is the official representative of Solidarités International in his/her intervention zone for NGOs, administrative, political and local authorities and civil society. He/She participates in humanitarian forums and relevant coordination meetings  
The FC Ensure that documents produced in his/her intervention zone meet deadlines and quality standards, respecting standard formats and procedures   
The FC Organise regular Base meetings and Ensure that key operational information circulates properly, in his/her intervention zone and between the bases and the country coordination (sitrep).

ISSUES AND SPECIFIC CHALLENGES :

Implement activities across several woredas in a volatile and operationally constrained context, while ensuring quality, compliance and timely delivery of ongoing projects. Maintain access and programme continuity despite recurrent constraints linked to fuel availability, cash liquidity, telecommunications/network coverage, road access and market fluctuations. Maintain adequate preparedness for a potential deterioration of the security situation, including possible disruption of banking services, communications and movements.

PRIORITIES ON THE 2-3 FIRST MONTHS :

-Consolidate the base management structure and ensure clear responsibilities, delegation and reporting lines within Programme and Support teams.   
-Ensure timely implementation and close monitoring of ongoing activities through updated workplans, APU/OFU/LFU and procurement plans.   
-Strengthen coordination between WASH, Livelihoods, MEAL and Support departments and ensure adequate balance of management capacity between the main programme components.   
-Reinforce budget forecasting and absorption monitoring.   
-Maintain and strengthen coordination with local authorities, clusters, partners and other humanitarian actors to avoid duplication and identify operational synergies.   
-Ensure the base is prepared for emergency scenarios through updated contingency plans, communication systems, cash/fuel contingency measures and staff preparedness, especially this year with the evolving context  
-Continue effort of base development with upcoming opportunities

SECURITY CONSTRAINTS :

The security environment in Tigray remains potentially volatile and can evolve rapidly, requiring continuous monitoring and strict compliance with SI security procedures. Main operational constraints include possible access restrictions, interruptions to telecommunications and internet, fuel shortages, banking/cash limitations and disruptions to road movements. Some operational areas may have limited or no network coverage, requiring reinforced movement tracking and communication procedures. The Field Coordinator must maintain a high level of preparedness, regularly review contingency arrangements, ensure critical resources are available, and adapt programme implementation and movements according to changes in the security and access environment. Staff safety and duty of care must remain central to operational decision-making.

YOUR PROFIL :

DIPLOMAS : A master’s degree (or equivalent field experience) in Humanitarian Action, International Development, Social Sciences, Project Management, or a related field is required.

EXPERIMENT IN THE HUMANITARIAN SECTOR : more than 5 years

EXPERIMENT ON SIMILAR POSITIONS : 3-4 years

TECHNICAL SKILLS :

Relevant management skills :Operation and team management skills include leadership, communication, and problem-solving as core competencies. Other essential skills are decision-making, time management, adaptability, and organizational abilities. Including a strong understanding of finance, and logistics processes.

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS : Ability to work under pressure in a challenging and sometimes insecure environment; cultural sensitivity, adaptability, and a strong commitment to humanitarian principles and safeguarding policies (PSEA, Child Protection).

LANGUAGES : Fluency in written and spoken English is essential. Knowledge of the local language(s) (e.g., Amharic, Tigrigna) is a strong asset.

SI WILL OFFER YOU :

**A salaried position:**

  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 3080 gross per month (2800 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 400.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**Living conditions:**

Guest House conditions :

\- There will be shared guesthouse both at the project and coordination during the visit.  
-Internet and telephone network : Available both in Addis and Adwa  
-Restaurant & social life: Restaurants are available in Addis and also Adwa :

\- Social life in Adwa is limited. All the basics food items and other are available but there is strict limitations and taxation to importation of food. Food in your luggage however is allowed and you can stock up on specials from home. Good quality chocolate, cereals and dried meat products can be hard to find and/or very expensive.

**Job Overview:** The Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other qualified immigrants to support a positive resettlement experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency . The Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Coordinate timely pre- and post-arrival services to ensure each client has essentials such as airport pick up upon arrival, initial and permanent housing, food, medical care, access to transportation, and is oriented to their new environment.
- Conduct intake services with clients to assess needs. Develop individualized self-sufficiency plans and SMART goals in partnership with each client.
- Provide services that are relevant to the client’s goals, including the distribution of direct financial assistance, applications for public benefits, referrals to medical and mental health services, and housing. Ensure active clients receive at meaningful interactions over the course of the service delivery period in accordance with program requirements.
